items.script:
Host: I’ve heard theaters have someone who displays subtitles in time with the spoken lines. I thought the subtitles appeared automatically once the script had been entered.
Operator: Even in the same play, the length of an actor’s pauses and the audience’s laughter varies from performance to performance. If subtitles appear too early, the audience may learn how an event ends before the actor says it.
Host: Does that mean you type all the subtitles afresh during the performance?
Operator: We prepare the sentences beforehand and divide them by scene. During the performance, we listen to the actors’ phrasing and display the corresponding section. items.script:
Host: In this exhibition, you ask visitors to write down memories evoked by a scent. That’s different from trying to identify its name. What is your intention?
Curator: The same scent may remind one person of an old bookshop and another of a sports field after rain. If we give visitors the scent’s name first, they may try to find that answer rather than draw on their own experience. That is why we have them read the explanation after the experience.
Host: Do you also exhibit the memories visitors write down?
Curator: We display only writing whose authors have agreed, and we do so anonymously. Seeing different accounts side by side shows how a single sensation can connect to diverse experiences. However, anyone who finds smelling the scents uncomfortable can participate just by reading other visitors’ accounts. This exhibition is not a test of the ability to distinguish smells.

items.script:
Host: In this exhibition, you ask visitors to write down memories evoked by a scent. That’s different from trying to identify its name. What is your intention?
Curator: The same scent may remind one person of an old bookshop and another of a sports field after rain. If we give visitors the scent’s name first, they may try to find that answer rather than draw on their own experience. That is why we have them read the explanation after the experience.
Host: Do you also exhibit the memories visitors write down?
Curator: We display only writing whose authors have agreed, and we do so anonymously. Seeing different accounts side by side shows how a single sensation can connect to diverse experiences. However, anyone who finds smelling the scents uncomfortable can participate just by reading other visitors’ accounts. This exhibition is not a test of the ability to distinguish smells.

Moderator: Let’s discuss opening government-office parking lots to residents when they are empty on weekends. We’ll hear from the supporter first.
Supporter: Spaces needed on weekdays are empty on weekends. Opening them is worthwhile because it could reduce parking shortages on nearby roads. However, vehicles must be removed on Sunday night so Monday’s work is not disrupted.
Reviewer: I agree with the aim of making use of the space. But instructions to remove cars alone may not ensure parking is available on Monday morning. We must first decide who will check and how to respond when departure deadlines are not observed.
Supporter: Then how about registering the vehicles using the lot and recording cases of cars not leaving during a trial period?
Reviewer: Those records would let us judge whether the staffing and procedures can actually handle the task. It would be best to decide how widely to open the lots after seeing those results.

主持人: 下面讨论把周末空着的机关停车场向居民开放的方案。请支持方先发言。
支持者: 平日需要的空间到了周末却空着。开放可以缓解周边道路的停车困难，所以值得实行。不过，需要规定星期日晚上必须把车开走，以免影响星期一的工作。

items.script: Lecturer: Does making an accurate map mean reproducing everything in a real space exactly? Showing every building and tree with equal emphasis may actually make it harder to find the route you need. For example, subway maps sometimes shorten or lengthen actual distances between stations in the drawing to make transfer connections easier to understand. On a walking-route map for wheelchair users, meanwhile, a route avoiding stairs matters more than a short route. Gradients and elevator locations should then stand out on the map. Even if two maps of the same area differ, neither one is necessarily wrong. The information kept and omitted depends on the decisions the user needs to make.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 지도를 정확하게 만든다는 것은 실제 공간의 모든 것을 그대로 옮긴다는 뜻일까요? 모든 건물과 나무를 같은 비중으로 표시하면 오히려 필요한 길을 찾기 어려울 수 있습니다. 예를 들어 지하철 노선도는 역 사이의 실제 거리를 줄이거나 늘려 그리기도 하지만, 환승 관계를 쉽게 파악하도록 만듭니다. 한편 휠체어 이용자를 위한 보행 지도에서는 짧은 길보다 계단을 피할 수 있는 길이 중요합니다. 이때는 경사나 승강기의 위치가 지도에서 눈에 잘 띄어야 합니다. 같은 지역의 지도 두 장이 서로 다르더라도 어느 하나가 반드시 잘못된 것은 아닙니다. 이용자가 어떤 판단을 내려야 하는지에 따라 남길 정보와 덜어 낼 정보가 달라지기 때문입니다.

items.script:
Reporter: This is where residents collect litter from the stream every week. Today, a new record board stands beside the scale used to weigh the rubbish bags. Let’s speak to the coordinator. Why record the number of participants and working time as well as the weight collected?
Coordinator: Last month, we thought the stream had become cleaner because the amount collected had fallen. But when we looked back at the records, rainy days had fewer participants and shorter working times. We could not conclude from the amount collected alone that the stream’s condition had improved.
Reporter: How do you plan to compare the results in future?
Coordinator: First, we will collect litter along the same stretch for a fixed length of time. We will also record participant numbers and weather, and examine days with substantially different conditions separately.
Reporter: Alongside removing rubbish, the residents are creating records that help them properly interpret changes at the site.

items.script:
记者: 这里是居民每周清理河道垃圾的现场。今天，称垃圾袋的秤旁边摆上了新的记录板。我们来采访一下负责人。除了收集重量，为什么还记录参与人数和工作时间呢？

Coordinator: Last month, we thought the stream had become cleaner because the amount collected had fallen. Host: Sometimes we feel we understand everything while reading a book, but cannot explain it when asked. How should we check our learning?
Professor: An explanation feeling familiar in front of you is different from being able to retrieve and use its content yourself. Close the book and represent the key relationships in words or a diagram. Where your explanation breaks down tells you what to revisit.
Host: Can we skip checking questions we answered correctly?
Professor: You may have chosen correctly by chance. Explaining why that answer is right and the others are not reveals what you understand and what you do not. items.script: Lecturer: When classifying things in nature, we must first decide what we want to compare. For example, the same rock specimen may belong to different groups in a class that sorts specimens by color and in research that analyzes their composition. This is because the classification criteria differ. Also, if the properties of the actual objects vary continuously, we must decide where to draw the boundary of a category. Difficulty placing a specimen at the boundary in either group does not make the entire classification useless. Rather, such specimens reveal the gap between the boundaries we create and the actual objects. If we forcibly remove these borderline cases or hide them in the nearest category, we also conceal the limitations of the criteria. If we disclose the criteria used and mark borderline cases separately, other researchers can compare the same data or regroup them for a new purpose. Classification can be described less as attaching permanent labels to objects than as making the basis for comparison explicit.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 자연의 대상을 분류할 때는 먼저 무엇을 비교하려는지 정해야 합니다. 예를 들어 암석 표본을 색에 따라 나누는 수업과, 어떤 성분이 들어 있는지 분석하는 연구에서는 같은 표본의 소속이 달라질 수 있습니다. 분류 기준이 다르기 때문입니다. 또 실제 대상의 성질이 연속적으로 변한다면 어디까지를 한 범주로 볼지도 결정해야 합니다. 경계에 놓인 표본을 어느 쪽에도 넣기 어렵다고 해서 분류 전체가 쓸모없는 것은 아닙니다. 오히려 그런 표본은 우리가 만든 경계와 실제 대상 사이의 차이를 드러냅니다. 이때 경계 사례를 억지로 지우거나 가장 가까운 범주에 감추면 기준의 한계까지 가려집니다. 사용한 기준을 공개하고 경계 사례를 따로 표시해 두면, 다른 연구자가 같은 자료를 비교하거나 새로운 목적에 맞게 다시 나눌 수 있습니다. 분류는 대상에 영구적인 이름표를 붙이는 일이라기보다, 비교의 기준을 드러내는 작업이라고 할 수 있습니다.

items.script:
Narrator: We are at a performance venue in an island village. Residents are practicing to bring to the stage songs once sung while rowing boats. At first, they joined together only the fast sections that would appeal to tourists. But a former fisher says something important is missing from the song.
Former fisher: The force used to put an oar into the water differs from the force used to pull it back. When the lead call was drawn out, those rowing together prepared for the next movement. If you only listen to the sound without doing the work, it is hard to understand why that passage was sung at length.
Narrator: Instead of recreating actual fishing work, the residents added rowing movements and short explanations to the song on stage. This allowed the audience to see the relationship between the sounds they heard and the movements of the body. They also arranged time to talk with the former fisher after the performance. For them, passing the song on does not end with preserving its pitches exactly. It means sharing with today’s audiences how the song made people move together.

items.script:
解说员: 这里是一个海岛村庄的演出场地。居民们正在排练，准备把从前划船时唱的歌搬上舞台。起初，他们只把适合唱给游客听的快节奏部分拼接起来。可是，一位曾经的渔民说，这首歌缺少了重要的东西。
曾经的渔民: 把桨放入水中和往回拉时，用力是不一样的。当领唱的声音拉长时，一起划船的人就会准备下一个动作。不实际做这些活，只听声音，就很难理解为什么那一段要唱得长。
解说员: 居民们没有重现实际的捕鱼作业，而是在舞台上为歌曲加上划桨动作和简短说明，让观众能够看见听到的声音与身体动作之间的关系。演出后，还安排了与那位曾经的渔民交谈的时间。对他们来说，传承歌曲不止是原样保存音的高低，也是与今天的观众分享这首歌怎样让人们一起行动。

items.script:
Narrator: We are at a performance venue in an island village. Residents are practicing to bring to the stage songs once sung while rowing boats. At first, they joined together only the fast sections that would appeal to tourists. But a former fisher says something important is missing from the song.
Former fisher: The force used to put an oar into the water differs from the force used to pull it back. When the lead call was drawn out, those rowing together prepared for the next movement. If you only listen to the sound without doing the work, it is hard to understand why that passage was sung at length.
Narrator: Instead of recreating actual fishing work, the residents added rowing movements and short explanations to the song on stage. This allowed the audience to see the relationship between the sounds they heard and the movements of the body. They also arranged time to talk with the former fisher after the performance. For them, passing the song on does not end with preserving its pitches exactly. It means sharing with today’s audiences how the song made people move together.

items.script: Lecturer: What needs to be the same for components from different companies to be used together? There is no need to standardize every part of their internal structure. If we agree on the dimensions of the parts that meet and the way they connect, the components can be combined even if their internal technologies differ. Such common standards do more than restrict freedom in development: they offer predictability about connecting with other products. Of course, this does not mean that a standard, once set, must be maintained forever. Sometimes a standard must change to accommodate new functions. However, the fact that a new standard is technically better does not by itself allow an immediate switch. Products and working methods have already been built around the existing standard. When making a change, we must decide how long existing products can remain connected. We must also decide what mechanisms will support the transition. The value of a standard lies not only in remaining unchanged. It also lies in allowing people to anticipate the scope and timing of changes and prepare for them.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 여러 회사의 부품을 함께 사용할 수 있게 하려면 무엇을 같게 해야 할까요? 모든 내부 구조를 통일할 필요는 없습니다. 서로 맞닿는 부분의 크기와 연결 방식을 합의하면, 안쪽의 기술은 서로 다르더라도 조합이 가능해집니다. 이런 공통 규격은 개발의 자유를 줄이기만 하는 것이 아니라, 다른 제품과 연결될 수 있다는 예측 가능성을 제공합니다. 물론 한번 정한 규격을 영원히 유지해야 한다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 새 기능을 담으려면 규격을 바꿔야 할 때도 있습니다. 다만 새 규격이 기술적으로 더 낫다는 사실만으로 즉시 전환할 수 있는 것은 아닙니다. 이미 그 규격을 바탕으로 만들어진 제품과 작업 방식이 있기 때문입니다. 변경할 때는 기존 제품이 어느 기간까지 연결될 수 있는지, 전환을 돕는 장치는 무엇인지 함께 정해야 합니다. 규격의 가치는 바뀌지 않는 데에만 있지 않습니다. 사람들이 변화의 범위와 시점을 예상하며 준비할 수 있도록 하는 데에도 있습니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 要让不同公司的零部件能够一起使用，需要把什么统一起来呢？没有必要统一所有内部结构。只要就相接部分的尺寸和连接方式达成一致，即使内部技术不同，也能组合使用。这种共同规格并不只是限制开发自由，也使人们能够预期产品可以与其他产品连接。当然，这不意味着一旦确定规格，就必须永远保持不变。为了容纳新功能，有时也需要改变规格。但新规格在技术上更好，并不意味着仅凭这一点就能立即切换，因为已经有基于原有规格制造的产品和相应的工作方式。变更时，必须确定现有产品可以连接使用到什么时候，也必须同时确定用什么措施帮助转换。规格的价值不仅在于不变，也在于让人们能够预知变化的范围和时间，并做好准备。

items.script:
Host: In your film, you leave some fairly long stretches after questions when no one says anything. Why did you keep that time in, even though viewers might find it frustrating?
Director: If we remove all the silences during editing, it looks as if the interviewee answered without hesitation. But some words come only after a long hesitation. I think the time it takes someone to say those words is as much a clue to understanding that person as the content of the answer. Viewers may understand the very same answer differently depending on whether it was offered readily or was difficult to say.
Host: Does that mean your principle is to show all the silences without editing them?
Director: Not quite. There is no need to retain even the pauses caused by adjusting equipment. I consider whether a hesitation affects how the account should be understood and retain it on that basis. Conversely, even if a silence actually occurred, stretching it out or placing it after a different question can create hesitation that was not originally there. So it is not enough merely to establish that there was a silence. We also need to look at which question it followed and how it connects to the words that come after it. What matters is preserving the relationship between speech and silence, rather than increasing the time when nothing is happening on screen.

主持人: 导演，您的影片在提问之后，保留了相当长的无人说话的片段。观众可能会觉得不耐烦，您仍然保留这段时间，有什么原因吗？
导演: 如果在剪辑时把沉默全都删掉，受访者就会显得回答得毫不迟疑。可是，有些话是犹豫了很久才说出口的。我认为，说出这些话所花的时间，和回答的内容一样，都是理解这个人的线索。因为即使是同样的回答，观众也可能根据那是毫不迟疑地说出的话，还是艰难说出的话，产生不同的理解。
主持人: 那么，您的原则是完全不剪辑沉默，把它们全部呈现出来吗？

导演: 如果在剪辑时把沉默全都删掉，受访者就会显得回答得毫不迟疑。可是，有些话是犹豫了很久才说出口的。我认为，说出这些话所花的时间，和回答的内容一样，都是理解这个人的线索。因为即使是同样的回答，观众也可能根据那是毫不迟疑地说出的话，还是艰难说出的话，产生不同的理解。
主持人: 那么，您的原则是完全不剪辑沉默，把它们全部呈现出来吗？
导演: 并不是这样。没有必要连调整设备造成的空白都保留下来。我会考察这种犹豫是否影响人们对所述内容的理解，并据此决定是否保留。反过来说，即使是真实发生过的沉默，如果将它拉长，或者接到另一个问题之后，也可能制造出原本没有的犹豫。因此，仅仅确认曾经有过沉默还不够，还需要看它发生在哪个问题之后，以及与随后说出的话有什么联系。重要的是保留话语与沉默之间的关系，而不是增加画面上什么都没有发生的时间。

transcriptTurns.textKo: 감독님 영화에는 질문 뒤에 아무 말도 하지 않는 장면이 꽤 오래 남아 있습니다. 관객이 답답해할 수 있는데도 그 시간을 남긴 이유가 있습니까?
transcriptTurns.speaker: 主持人
transcriptTurns.text: 导演，您的影片在提问之后，保留了相当长的无人说话的片段。观众可能会觉得不耐烦，您仍然保留这段时间，有什么原因吗？

transcriptTurns.textKo: 편집할 때 침묵을 모두 덜어 내면 인터뷰한 사람이 막힘없이 답한 것처럼 보입니다. 그러나 어떤 말은 오래 망설인 끝에 나옵니다. 저는 답의 내용만큼 그 말을 꺼내기까지 걸린 시간도 그 사람을 이해하는 단서라고 봅니다. 관객은 같은 답변이라도 선뜻 한 말인지 어렵게 꺼낸 말인지에 따라 다르게 받아들일 수 있으니까요.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 그렇다면 침묵은 편집하지 않고 전부 보여 주는 것이 원칙입니까?

items.script: Lecturer: When reading a novel, it is easy to immediately accept what the narrator explains as established fact within the fictional world. Yet the narrator’s knowledge may be limited. Let us consider a short imagined scene. During a presentation, the protagonist sees a friend’s empty seat and thinks that the friend left because they disagreed with the protagonist’s opinion. Later, the reader learns that the friend received an urgent phone call and went out into the hallway. Can we immediately call the first account a deliberate lie? If the protagonist did not see the friend taking the call, the judgment may have been based on limited information. In this way, not every account that is later corrected comes from an intention to deceive the reader. What matters is not just the content of an account but also how the information was obtained. We must distinguish who saw what directly, whether they heard it from someone else, and whether they added their own feelings to observed facts. Only then can we judge how to reread earlier scenes when new information emerges.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 소설을 읽을 때 서술자가 설명하는 내용을 곧바로 작품 세계의 확정된 사실로 받아들이기 쉽습니다. 그러나 서술자가 알 수 있는 범위가 제한된 경우도 있습니다. 짧은 가상 장면을 보겠습니다. 주인공은 발표 도중 친구의 빈자리를 보고, 친구가 자신의 의견에 반대해 자리를 떠났다고 생각합니다. 나중에 독자는 그 친구가 급한 전화를 받아 복도에 나갔다는 사실을 알게 됩니다. 여기서 첫 설명을 곧바로 의도적인 거짓말이라고 부를 수 있을까요? 주인공이 친구가 전화를 받는 모습을 보지 못했다면, 제한된 정보로 내린 판단이었을 수 있습니다. 이처럼 서술 내용이 뒤에 수정된다고 해서 모두 독자를 속이려는 의도에서 나온 것은 아닙니다. 중요한 것은 그 설명의 내용뿐 아니라 정보가 생긴 경로입니다. 누가 무엇을 직접 보았는지, 다른 사람에게 전해 들었는지, 관찰한 사실에 자신의 감정을 덧붙였는지를 구별해야 합니다. 그래야 새 정보가 나왔을 때 앞선 장면을 어떻게 다시 읽어야 하는지 판단할 수 있습니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 读小说时，人们容易直接把叙述者说明的内容当作作品世界中已经确定的事实。然而，叙述者所能知道的范围有时是有限的。来看一个简短的虚构场景。主人公在发言过程中看到朋友的空座位，就认为朋友是因为反对自己的意见而离席的。后来，读者得知那位朋友接到紧急电话，才走到了走廊上。这里能立即把最初的解释称为故意说谎吗？如果主人公没看到朋友接电话的情景，那可能只是依据有限信息作出的判断。像这样，不能因为叙述内容后来被修正，就认为它全都出于欺骗读者的意图。重要的不只是解释的内容，还有信息的获取途径。必须区分谁直接看到了什么、是否从他人那里听说，以及是否在观察到的事实中加入了自己的情感。只有这样，才能在新信息出现时判断应当如何重新阅读前面的场景。

transcriptTurns.text: 读小说时，人们容易直接把叙述者说明的内容当作作品世界中已经确定的事实。然而，叙述者所能知道的范围有时是有限的。来看一个简短的虚构场景。主人公在发言过程中看到朋友的空座位，就认为朋友是因为反对自己的意见而离席的。后来，读者得知那位朋友接到紧急电话，才走到了走廊上。这里能立即把最初的解释称为故意说谎吗？如果主人公没看到朋友接电话的情景，那可能只是依据有限信息作出的判断。像这样，不能因为叙述内容后来被修正，就认为它全都出于欺骗读者的意图。重要的不只是解释的内容，还有信息的获取途径。必须区分谁直接看到了什么、是否从他人那里听说，以及是否在观察到的事实中加入了自己的情感。只有这样，才能在新信息出现时判断应当如何重新阅读前面的场景。

Resident: Someone who arrived after me was using a workbench first. Has the queue order changed?
Operator: We have slightly changed the system of assigning all the workbenches in arrival order. When long repairs kept coming, even people who only wanted to tighten one screw had to wait a long time. Now we set aside one workbench for tasks that can be finished within ten minutes.

Operator: The other two workbenches follow the existing numbered queue. Only when there are no short tasks can we accept long tasks at the separate workbench as well. We do not stop a task once it has begun.
Resident: So you are trying to reduce the inconvenience of everyone waiting in a single queue despite needing different amounts of time.

items.script:
Host: Wouldn’t recording the actual object shown on screen produce the most realistic sound?
Sound creator: Sound made that way does not necessarily come across well in the scene. In this film, the actor sets down a heavy box, but the box used for filming was light. Using its sound would lose the sense of weight the audience should feel. I layered a brief scraping sound over a low resonance to create the feeling of the box pressing down on the floor.
Host: Does that mean you do not use sounds recorded on location?
Sound creator: I use them as they are if they convey the character’s movement and the sense of the space sufficiently. But I do not choose a sound just because it sounds impressive on its own. If it stands out too much when played with the dialogue, it can actually overshadow the character’s action. My criterion is what it makes the audience feel within the scene, rather than which object actually produced it.

Host: Wouldn’t recording the actual object shown on screen produce the most realistic sound?
Sound creator: Sound made that way does not necessarily come across well in the scene. In this film, the actor sets down a heavy box, but the box used for filming was light. Using its sound would lose the sense of weight the audience should feel. I layered a brief scraping sound over a low resonance to create the feeling of the box pressing down on the floor.
Host: Does that mean you do not use sounds recorded on location?
Sound creator: I use them as they are if they convey the character’s movement and the sense of the space sufficiently. But I do not choose a sound just because it sounds impressive on its own. If it stands out too much when played with the dialogue, it can actually overshadow the character’s action. My criterion is what it makes the audience feel within the scene, rather than which object actually produced it.

Woman: You want us to take the side we disagree with in the next exercise? I think arguing for something I do not believe would sound awkward.
Man: The aim is not to make you change your mind. If you always look only for material supporting your own side, it is easy to miss why the other side reaches its conclusion. When you switch roles, you have to start by identifying the conditions those people consider important.
Woman: So it is an exercise to make it easier to find weaknesses in the opposing argument.

items.script:
Host: The studio wall is covered with small ceramic tiles. Are they samples showing the colors of the vessels you will sell?
Potter: I do show them to customers, but for me they are records for comparing working conditions. Even with the same glaze, different types of clay or different coating thicknesses can sometimes produce a color other than the one I expected. So on the back I write not only the names of the clay and glaze, but also the number of coats and the position in the kiln.
Host: You have kept tiles that did not produce the color you wanted, too.
Potter: If I kept only the colors I wanted, I could not compare why the other results occurred. However, I do not apply a combination that succeeded here directly to a large vessel. A different shape can change the way the glaze flows, so I test it once more on a small vessel. The records establish a starting point for new work, but do not guarantee the result.

items.script:
Moderator: The free exhibition has become popular, so we need to discuss how to allocate admission places. Please comment on the proposal to expand advance reservations.
Panelist A: We should reduce cases in which people queue for a long time only to be unable to enter. Reservations let visitors plan their visits, so I think most places should be allocated in advance.
Panelist B: I agree with reducing wasted trips. However, people unfamiliar with online reservations may lose out in the competition to connect. We should retain a fixed allocation for walk-ins and let people check that day’s remaining number even from outside the entrance.

items.script: Lecturer: It is easy to feel reassured when a “backup complete” indicator appears beside your work file. But having a copy is different from being able to resume work when you need to. Keeping several copies under different folder names on the same storage device may help if you accidentally delete a file. However, if that device fails, the copies will become inaccessible too. Even a copy stored elsewhere may not serve its intended purpose if its contents were copied incorrectly or you do not have a program that can open it. So when checking backups, do not stop at counting them. Assume the original is unavailable and actually try restoring a few representative files at a separate location. Success in this test once is not the end of the matter. A change in the file formats or tools you use gives you a reason to check again. You do not need to restore every file daily, but you should not rely solely on an old success indicator when the conditions your work requires have changed. The purpose of backup is not to finish the act of copying, but to leave a way to resume interrupted work.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 작업 파일 옆에 백업 완료라는 표시가 뜨면 안심하기 쉽습니다. 하지만 복사본이 있다는 사실과 필요할 때 작업을 다시 시작할 수 있다는 것은 다릅니다. 같은 저장 장치 안에 폴더 이름만 달리해 여러 부를 두었다면 파일 하나를 잘못 지웠을 때에는 도움이 될 수 있습니다. 그러나 그 장치가 고장 나면 복사본도 함께 열 수 없게 됩니다. 다른 장소에 둔 복사본도 내용이 잘못 복사되었거나 그 파일을 열 프로그램이 없다면 기대한 역할을 못 할 수 있습니다. 그래서 백업을 점검할 때는 개수를 세는 데서 그치지 않고, 원본을 쓸 수 없다는 상황을 가정해 별도의 장소에서 대표 파일 몇 개를 실제로 복구해 봐야 합니다. 이 시험을 한 번 성공했다고 끝나는 것도 아닙니다. 사용하는 파일 형식이나 작업 도구가 바뀌면 다시 확인할 이유가 생깁니다. 모든 파일을 매일 복원할 필요는 없지만, 자신의 작업에 필요한 조건이 바뀌었는데도 예전의 성공 표시만 믿어서는 곤란합니다. 백업의 목적은 복사 행위를 마치는 것이 아니라, 중단된 일을 다시 할 수 있는 길을 남기는 데 있습니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 工作文件旁出现“备份完成”的标记时，人们很容易就放心了。但有副本，与需要时能重新开展工作，是两回事。在同一存储设备上，只用不同文件夹名称保存多份副本，误删一个文件时或许能帮上忙。然而，设备一旦损坏，副本也会一起无法打开。即使副本保存在别处，如果内容复制有误，或没有能打开该文件的程序，也可能无法发挥预期作用。因此检查备份不能只数数量，还要假设原文件无法使用，在另一地点实际恢复几个有代表性的文件。这样的测试成功一次，也不代表就结束了。如果使用的文件格式或工作工具改变，就有理由再次检查。无须每天恢复全部文件，但工作所需条件已经变化时，不能仍只相信过去的成功标记。备份的目的不是完成复制动作，而是为中断的工作留下能够重新开展的途径。

items.script: Lecturer: It is easy to feel reassured when a “backup complete” indicator appears beside your work file. But having a copy is different from being able to resume work when you need to. Keeping several copies under different folder names on the same storage device may help if you accidentally delete a file. However, if that device fails, the copies will become inaccessible too. Even a copy stored elsewhere may not serve its intended purpose if its contents were copied incorrectly or you do not have a program that can open it. So when checking backups, do not stop at counting them. Assume the original is unavailable and actually try restoring a few representative files at a separate location. Success in this test once is not the end of the matter. A change in the file formats or tools you use gives you a reason to check again. You do not need to restore every file daily, but you should not rely solely on an old success indicator when the conditions your work requires have changed. The purpose of backup is not to finish the act of copying, but to leave a way to resume interrupted work.

items.script:
Reporter: The cultural center’s recording room frequently had to stop sessions because of corridor noise. Yet I hear recording has become much easier without building new walls. What changed?
Manager: At first we asked everyone to keep the whole corridor quiet. But desks for classes on the same floor still had to be moved, and cleaning had to be done, so requests alone did not solve it. Logging when the noise occurred showed that most of it coincided with moving desks and cleaning the floor after the morning classes.
Reporter: Did you move the classes to another floor?
Manager: The classes are in the same place. Instead, we adjusted the work sequence so moving and cleaning are finished before the first afternoon recording. We also review the recording schedule together with the staff doing that work. If a repair is suddenly scheduled, we contact the people with reservations first and let them choose their recording times.
Reporter: So the building does not block sound any better, but you have reduced the times when necessary activities conflict.

items.script:
记者: 文化中心的录音室过去经常因为走廊噪声而中断使用。不过听说没有重新建墙，录音就顺利了很多，发生了什么变化？

items.script:
Host: Beginners can easily think they do not need to practice the sections where their own instrument is silent. Why are bars of rest important?
Conductor: If you only count until your turn, you can miss the flow of the other instruments. The tempo you settled on when practicing alone also varies a little in an ensemble. During rests, you need to listen to which instrument carries the melody and understand how your own sound follows it.
Host: Then should they stop counting beats and simply follow the other instruments?
Conductor: Counting beats is fundamental. I am suggesting adding audible cues to it. First, I have them quietly sing the melody that occurs while their own part rests. Next, holding their instrument, they connect the moment that melody ends with their first note. To prevent entering immediately on hearing a familiar sound, they also check which repetition it is when the same melody recurs.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose a research team has recorded dust concentrations in a workshop for several years. If the readings fall after the measuring device is replaced one year, can we say the air became cleaner from that year onward? We first need to know whether the new device gives the same readings as the old one under the same conditions. This is because the effect of a changed measurement method and actual environmental change coincide at one point in time. Rather than immediately removing the old device, the team operated both devices together at the same location for a period. The readings were similar when dust levels were low, but the difference grew when they were high. In this case, adjusting the two records by subtracting a single number is not appropriate. Using the overlapping observations, we need to examine the range in which the difference grows and state the range within which comparisons are valid. The replacement date and device characteristics must also be recorded so later users of the data do not immediately mistake a break in the readings for environmental change. Using newer equipment and meaningfully continuing a long-running record are separate tasks.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 한 연구팀이 작업실의 먼지 농도를 여러 해 동안 기록했다고 합시다. 어느 해 측정기를 새것으로 바꾼 뒤 수치가 낮아졌다면, 그해부터 공기가 깨끗해졌다고 말할 수 있을까요? 새 장비가 이전 장비와 같은 조건에서 같은 수치를 내는지 먼저 알아야 합니다. 측정 방식이 달라진 효과와 실제 환경의 변화가 한 시점에 겹쳐 있기 때문입니다. 연구팀은 옛 장비를 바로 치우지 않고 일정 기간 두 장비를 같은 장소에서 함께 작동시켰습니다. 그러자 먼지가 적을 때는 두 값이 비슷하지만 많을 때는 차이가 커졌습니다. 이런 경우 두 기록의 차이를 하나의 숫자로 빼서 맞추는 방법은 적절하지 않습니다. 겹쳐 관측한 자료를 통해 어느 범위에서 차이가 커지는지 살펴보고, 비교 가능한 범위를 밝혀야 합니다. 또 바꾼 날짜와 장비 특성을 기록에 남겨야 나중에 자료를 쓰는 사람이 수치의 꺾임을 곧바로 환경 변화로 오해하지 않습니다. 더 새 장비를 쓰는 것과 오래된 기록을 의미 있게 이어 가는 것은 별개의 과제입니다.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose a research team has recorded dust concentrations in a workshop for several years. If the readings fall after the measuring device is replaced one year, can we say the air became cleaner from that year onward? We first need to know whether the new device gives the same readings as the old one under the same conditions. This is because the effect of a changed measurement method and actual environmental change coincide at one point in time. Rather than immediately removing the old device, the team operated both devices together at the same location for a period. The readings were similar when dust levels were low, but the difference grew when they were high. In this case, adjusting the two records by subtracting a single number is not appropriate. Using the overlapping observations, we need to examine the range in which the difference grows and state the range within which comparisons are valid. The replacement date and device characteristics must also be recorded so later users of the data do not immediately mistake a break in the readings for environmental change. Using newer equipment and meaningfully continuing a long-running record are separate tasks.

items.script:
Commentator: An old vessel sits on a museum workbench. Small pieces of metal are embedded along its cracks. To someone seeing it for the first time, they might look like parts that should be removed to restore the original appearance. The person in charge, however, records them in detail.
Conservation officer: These are traces of repairs made so the broken vessel could be used again. They were not part of its original appearance, but they tell us that it continued to be used after breaking once. If we focus only on making the surface smooth, that period of its history disappears.
Commentator: Does that mean leaving all the attached traces untouched?
Conservation officer: We also need to examine whether changes in the metal are pushing against the vessel again. Parts currently causing damage are documented and then treated to stabilize them. And we do not conclude from this repair alone that the owner was poor or especially attached to the vessel. The fact that it continued to be used and why that was done are different questions.
Commentator: This work is not simply about recovering the moment when an object was first made. It examines both the meaning of surviving traces and present safety, distinguishing what they tell us from what remains unknown.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 박물관 작업대 위에 오래된 그릇 한 점이 놓여 있습니다. 깨진 틈을 따라 작은 금속 조각들이 박혀 있습니다. 처음 보는 사람에게는 원래 모습으로 돌리려면 떼어 내야 할 부품처럼 보일지 모릅니다. 그러나 담당자는 그 조각을 자세히 기록합니다.

items.script:
解说员: 博物馆的工作台上放着一件旧器皿，裂缝沿线嵌着小金属片。初次看到的人，或许会觉得为了恢复原貌应该把这些部件拆下。然而，负责人却在详细记录这些金属片。
保护负责人: 这是为了重新使用破损器皿而留下的修理痕迹。虽然不是最初制作时的样子，却说明这件器皿破损后仍被继续使用。若只专注于把表面变光滑，那段使用历史就会消失。
解说员: 那么，附着的痕迹都不处理，全部留下吗？
保护负责人: 也要检查金属发生变化后，是否又在挤压器皿。正在造成损伤的部分，会先记录状态，再作稳定处理。而且，不能仅凭这次修理就断定主人贫穷，或特别珍爱这件器皿。继续使用的事实，与为什么这样做，是两个不同的问题。
解说员: 这项工作并不只是找回最初制作的瞬间，还要兼顾现存痕迹的意义与当前的安全，区分它们能告诉我们的事与尚不可知的事。

items.script:
Commentator: An old vessel sits on a museum workbench. Small pieces of metal are embedded along its cracks. To someone seeing it for the first time, they might look like parts that should be removed to restore the original appearance. The person in charge, however, records them in detail.
Conservation officer: These are traces of repairs made so the broken vessel could be used again. They were not part of its original appearance, but they tell us that it continued to be used after breaking once. If we focus only on making the surface smooth, that period of its history disappears.
Commentator: Does that mean leaving all the attached traces untouched?
Conservation officer: We also need to examine whether changes in the metal are pushing against the vessel again. Parts currently causing damage are documented and then treated to stabilize them. And we do not conclude from this repair alone that the owner was poor or especially attached to the vessel. The fact that it continued to be used and why that was done are different questions.
Commentator: This work is not simply about recovering the moment when an object was first made. It examines both the meaning of surviving traces and present safety, distinguishing what they tell us from what remains unknown.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose scarce free passes for a shared workshop are distributed to people who queue from dawn. Can we say everyone has the same opportunity because no money is charged? Even the same hour imposes a different burden on someone who must work then and someone who can rearrange their schedule. In this system, the ability to spend time waiting replaces price as a criterion for allocation. But we cannot immediately conclude that selling the passes would be fairer, because differences in ability to pay would then matter. One alternative is to accept applications over a set period, draw lots, and reallocate a pass if the selected person does not confirm that they will use it. This offers an opportunity to apply even without the flexibility to queue early, but it does not select people with a greater need to use the workshop. If the degree of need is to take priority, separate criteria and a verification process are required. When evaluating an allocation method, we should consider more than whether it is free: we must identify what abilities or conditions it actually requires and what it prioritizes.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 공유 작업실의 무료 이용권이 부족할 때 새벽부터 줄 선 사람에게 나누어 준다고 합시다. 돈을 받지 않으니 누구에게나 같은 기회라고 말할 수 있을까요? 같은 한 시간이라도 그 시간에 일을 해야 하는 사람과 일정을 바꿀 수 있는 사람에게 부담은 다릅니다. 이 방식에서는 가격 대신 기다릴 수 있는 여유가 배분의 기준에 들어갑니다. 그렇다고 곧바로 유료 판매가 더 공정하다고 결론 내릴 수도 없습니다. 그 경우에는 돈을 낼 수 있는 차이가 작용하기 때문입니다. 한 가지 대안은 일정 기간 신청을 받아 추첨하고, 선정된 사람이 사용을 확인하지 않으면 다시 배분하는 것입니다. 이것은 일찍 줄을 설 여유가 없어도 신청할 기회를 주지만, 이용 필요가 더 큰 사람을 골라내는 방식은 아닙니다. 만약 필요의 크기를 우선하려면 별도의 기준과 확인 절차가 있어야 합니다. 배분 방식을 평가할 때는 무료인지 아닌지만 볼 것이 아니라, 그 방식이 실제로 어떤 능력이나 조건을 요구하고 무엇을 우선하는지 밝혀야 합니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 假设共享工作室的免费使用券不足，就发给从清晨开始排队的人。不收钱，就能说每个人机会相同吗？同样一个小时，对当时必须工作的人与可以调整日程的人，负担并不相同。这种方式把有时间等待的条件，代替价格纳入了分配标准。但也不能马上得出收费出售更公平的结论，因为那时支付能力的差异又会产生作用。一种替代办法是在一定期间接受申请，再抽签；中签者若不确认使用，就重新分配。这让没有余裕早早排队的人也有申请机会，但并不是挑出使用需求更大者的方法。如果要优先考虑需求程度，就需要另外的标准和核实程序。评价分配方式时，不应只看是否免费，还应明确它实际要求什么能力或条件，以及优先考虑什么。

items.script:
Host: The costumes looked different in color in the studio, but almost the same on stage. Was the fabric chosen incorrectly?
Designer: That is why we cannot decide by looking at the fabric alone. The color and brightness of the light on the actors and the background behind them can weaken the differences between costumes. In this scene the two characters oppose each other, so their boundary needed to remain visible from a distance, but that effect disappeared.
Host: So did you make one character’s costume brighter?
Designer: We tried that first, but the bright fabric reflected too much light in the next scene. Instead, we kept the basic color and added a strip with a different texture along the edge of one costume. We decided after checking whether the silhouettes were distinguishable even from the back of the audience.
Host: So it is hard to judge just by finishing one costume on its own.
Designer: Yes. A costume can be beautiful on its own, but on stage it also helps show the relationships between characters. Even if it is clearly visible in one scene, it needs readjustment if it interferes with movement and light in another.

items.script:
主持人: 在工作室看到的服装颜色不同，到了舞台上却几乎一样。是面料选错了吗？
设计师: 这正是不能只看面料就决定的原因。演员所受灯光的颜色、亮度，以及背后的背景，都可能削弱服装之间的差别。这次是两个人物对立的场景，本应从远处也能看清两者的界线，但这种效果消失了。
主持人: 所以您把其中一个人的服装改得更亮了吗？
设计师: 起初试过，但明亮的布料在下一个场景里反光过强。所以我们保留基本颜色，在一边服装的边缘加了一条质感不同的带子，确认从观众席后方也能区分轮廓后才决定。

items.script: Lecturer: Sometimes a notice tells employees to be more careful in order to reduce repeated data-entry mistakes. But if the same mistake keeps occurring across several people, the input screen also needs examination. For example, if people confuse the quantity field with the packaging-unit field and order one item instead of one box, separating the two fields and showing the final item count together can reduce the chance of error. However, a system designed to block every unanticipated order creates a new problem: it cannot handle a special order requiring only a small quantity. Letting anyone turn off the warning and proceed to avoid this could make the original safeguard ineffective. A better method is to retain the structure that prevents confusion for ordinary orders, while routing exceptional orders through a separate review process that records the reason and the person who checked them. If exceptions recur frequently, rather than only counting employees’ rule violations, examine whether the basic rules sufficiently accommodate actual types of orders. A good procedure reduces routine errors while also leaving information that helps us recognize unexpected situations.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 반복되는 입력 실수를 줄이겠다며 직원에게 주의하라는 공지를 보내는 경우가 있습니다. 그러나 같은 실수가 여러 사람에게 계속 나타난다면 입력 화면도 살펴볼 필요가 있습니다. 예를 들어 수량 칸과 포장 단위 칸을 혼동해 한 상자를 한 개로 주문한다면, 두 칸을 떨어뜨리고 최종 개수를 함께 보여 주는 식으로 실수 가능성을 줄일 수 있습니다. 그런데 시스템이 예상하지 못한 주문을 전부 막는 방향으로 설계하면 새로운 문제가 생깁니다. 소량만 필요한 특별 주문도 처리하지 못하는 것이지요. 이를 피하려고 누구나 경고를 끄고 진행하게 하면 처음의 장치가 유명무실해질 수 있습니다. 더 나은 방법은 일반 주문에서는 혼동을 막는 구조를 유지하면서, 예외 주문은 이유와 확인자를 남겨 별도 경로로 검토하게 하는 것입니다. 예외가 자주 반복된다면 직원의 규정 위반 횟수만 세기보다 기본 규칙이 실제 주문 형태를 충분히 담고 있는지 점검해야 합니다. 좋은 절차는 평소의 실수를 줄이고, 예상 밖의 상황을 알아볼 수 있는 정보도 남깁니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 有时为了减少重复的输入错误，会发通知要求员工多加注意。但如果多人不断出现同一种错误，也有必要检查输入界面。例如，把数量栏与包装单位栏混淆，把一箱订成一个，就可以将两个栏位分开，并同时显示最终个数，以减少出错的可能性。然而，如果系统设计成拦截所有未预料到的订单，又会出现新问题：连只需少量的特殊订单也无法处理。若为避免这一点而允许任何人关闭警告继续操作，原有防错装置又可能形同虚设。更好的办法是在普通订单中保留防止混淆的结构，同时让例外订单记录理由与核实者，通过另外的流程审查。如果例外经常重复，就不应只统计员工违反规定的次数，还应检查基本规则是否充分涵盖实际订单类型。好的程序既减少日常错误，也留下有助于识别意外情况的信息。

items.script:
Woman: You’re going to place a model the same size as the sculpture beside it and let visitors touch it? Won’t visitors mistake the model for the real artwork?
Man: We will position the original and the model separately and put a large label on the model identifying it as such. Visitors cannot touch the original, but on the model they can trace even the deep groove at the back with their hands. It is a structure that is hard to make out just by looking from the front.
Woman: Couldn’t you add photographs of the back to the description?
Man: We plan to include photographs too. We simply want to offer a way to check the depth and the direction in which the groove continues by hand as well. The model will be made of a lightweight material, so we will also explain that its surface feels different from the original.
Woman: So you are not exhibiting it as a substitute, but providing another way to examine the form. That sounds fine if the model is clearly distinguished from the original and the material difference is explained.

items.script:
Host: In this puppet show, the people operating the puppets remain visible on stage. Won’t that make it harder for the audience to feel that the puppets are alive?
Director: We did have that concern. That is why the puppeteers avoid conspicuous facial acting and keep their gaze on the puppets. Even while seeing the human hands, the audience can follow how the puppet’s hesitation is created at the fingertips.
Host: So the audience also sees the technique that creates movement as part of the work.
Director: Yes. Removing the cloth that hid the puppeteers did not reduce rehearsal. Even small changes in force are visible, so the hand movements actually need more restraint. Rather than having the audience listen to explanations of technique, I wanted them to see the moment emotion becomes movement.

items.script: Lecturer: Let’s consider a hypothetical example to think about the order of survey questions. Suppose that before asking residents how satisfied they are with life in the neighborhood, we ask them to list three recent inconveniences. When they answer the overall satisfaction question, those inconveniences they just listed may come to mind first. Conversely, if we ask about positive experiences first, they will answer with different scenes in mind. We must not immediately interpret a difference in answers as a difference in residents’ lives. We also need to consider which memories the questionnaire brought to mind first. To examine this, we can randomly divide respondents recruited in the same way into two groups, asking one about specific experiences first and the other for an overall evaluation first. The other wording and survey conditions must stay the same to examine the effect of order. Even if the two results differ, this comparison alone cannot establish which represents residents’ true feelings.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 설문 문항의 순서를 생각하기 위해 가상의 사례를 보겠습니다. 주민에게 동네 생활이 얼마나 만족스러운지 묻기 전에, 최근 불편했던 일을 세 가지 적게 했다고 합시다. 종합 만족도에 답할 때 방금 적은 불편이 먼저 떠오를 수 있겠죠. 반대로 좋았던 일을 먼저 묻는다면 다른 장면을 떠올린 상태에서 답하게 됩니다. 이때 답의 차이를 곧바로 주민 생활의 차이로 읽어서는 안 됩니다. 질문지가 어느 기억을 먼저 불러냈는지도 살펴야 하기 때문입니다. 이를 확인하려면 같은 모집 방식으로 모은 응답자를 무작위로 두 집단에 나누고, 한쪽에는 세부 경험을 먼저, 다른 쪽에는 종합 평가를 먼저 묻게 할 수 있습니다. 다른 문구와 조사 조건은 같게 두어야 순서의 영향을 따져 볼 수 있습니다. 두 결과가 달라도 어느 쪽이 주민의 진짜 마음인지 이 비교만으로 확정할 수는 없습니다.

items.script: Lecturer: Let’s consider a hypothetical example to think about the order of survey questions. Suppose that before asking residents how satisfied they are with life in the neighborhood, we ask them to list three recent inconveniences. When they answer the overall satisfaction question, those inconveniences they just listed may come to mind first. Conversely, if we ask about positive experiences first, they will answer with different scenes in mind. We must not immediately interpret a difference in answers as a difference in residents’ lives. We also need to consider which memories the questionnaire brought to mind first. To examine this, we can randomly divide respondents recruited in the same way into two groups, asking one about specific experiences first and the other for an overall evaluation first. The other wording and survey conditions must stay the same to examine the effect of order. Even if the two results differ, this comparison alone cannot establish which represents residents’ true feelings.

items.script:
Reporter: We are at a hypothetical book festival. The display at the entrance shows 500 cumulative entries this morning and 100 people currently inside. Why are these two numbers different?
Manager: The cumulative entry count adds up the number of entries. For the current number of people, we subtract exits from entries, starting with an empty venue. So far there have been 500 entries and 400 exits, so there are 100 people inside.
Reporter: Why do you have this display?
Manager: How often people have come and gone during the day and how crowded it is inside now are different matters. Entrance staff use the current number to manage the flow of admissions. Looking only at cumulative entries would mean treating people who have already left as still inside.
Reporter: What happens if the same person briefly leaves and comes back in?
Manager: When they leave, we subtract one from the current number, and when they return, we add one. Their return also adds one new entry to the cumulative entry count. That is why we do not call that count the number of distinct people who visited today.

items.script:
记者: 这里是一个假设的图书节现场。入口电子显示屏显示，上午累计入场500次，目前场内有100人。这两个数字为什么不同？
管理人员: 累计入场数是把进入的次数相加。目前人数则从开始时为空的场地算起，用进入数减去离开数。到现在入场500次、离场400次，所以场内有100人。
记者: 设置这个显示屏是为什么呢？
管理人员: 一天里有多少进出和现在里面有多拥挤，是不同的问题。入口工作人员会看当前人数，调节入场人流。只看累计入场数，就会把已经离开的人也当成仍在里面。
记者: 同一个人暂时出去后又进来，会怎样计算？
管理人员: 出去时从当前人数减去一人，回来时再加一人。累计入场数也会把回来这一次计为一次新的入场。因此，我们不会用累计入场数表示今天来了多少位不同的访客。

记者: 这里是一个假设的图书节现场。入口电子显示屏显示，上午累计入场500次，目前场内有100人。这两个数字为什么不同？

Planner: I compared the proposed stands for the traveling exhibition. Adding the scores for color, price, and ease of storage puts Design 가 slightly ahead.
Maker: But Design 가 cannot fit through the transport vehicle’s door even when folded. Is that size a condition that other advantages can compensate for?

Maker: We have no budget to change the transport vehicle, and the stand has to be moved every week. So fitting through the door is a condition that must be met first. We can compare color and price among the designs that meet it. Design 가 can also be considered again if a smaller revised version is produced.
Planner: I see. The problem was adding transport feasibility into the calculation alongside the other criteria.

items.script: Lecturer: When comparing services, is the average waiting time enough? Suppose three people waited at each of two hypothetical counters. At Counter 가, all three waited five minutes. At Counter 나, two waited one minute each and the remaining person waited thirteen minutes. Both counters have exactly the same average of five minutes. However, for someone with little time before their next appointment, the two may not be equivalent choices. The possibility of a long wait matters as well as the possibility of finishing quickly. That does not mean Counter 나 is worse for everyone. Someone with time to spare may place more value on the chance of finishing quickly. An average summarizes one aspect of all the waiting times. To use it when choosing, we should also explain how evenly the waits are distributed and how much long waiting occurs. Also remember that these three people’s records alone cannot guarantee the next customer’s waiting time.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 서비스를 비교할 때 평균 대기 시간만 보면 충분할까요? 가상의 두 창구에서 세 명씩 기다렸다고 합시다. 가 창구에서는 세 사람 모두 오 분을 기다렸습니다. 나 창구에서는 두 사람이 각각 일 분, 나머지 한 사람이 십삼 분을 기다렸습니다. 두 창구의 평균은 똑같이 오 분입니다. 하지만 다음 약속까지 여유가 적은 사람에게 두 방식은 같은 선택이 아닐 수 있습니다. 짧게 끝날 가능성뿐 아니라 오래 기다릴 가능성도 중요하니까요. 그렇다고 나 창구가 누구에게나 나쁘다고 할 수도 없습니다. 시간 여유가 있는 사람은 짧게 끝날 가능성을 더 중시할 수 있죠. 평균은 전체 대기의 한 측면을 요약한 값입니다. 선택에 쓰려면 기다림이 얼마나 고르게 나뉘는지, 긴 대기가 어느 정도 생기는지도 함께 알려야 합니다. 이 세 사람의 기록만으로 다음 손님의 시간을 보장할 수는 없다는 점도 잊지 마십시오.

items.script: 演讲者: 比较服务时，只看平均等候时间就足够了吗？假设有两个虚构的服务窗口，各有三个人等候。가窗口的三个人都等了五分钟。나窗口有两个人各等一分钟，另外一个人等了十三分钟。两个窗口的平均值同样都是五分钟。但是，对于距下一项安排时间不多的人，两种方式可能并不是同样的选择。除了很快结束的可能性，长时间等候的可能性也很重要。不过，也不能说나窗口对所有人都更差。时间充裕的人可能更重视很快结束的机会。平均值只概括了整体等候情况的一个方面。用于作选择时，还应说明等候时间分布是否均匀，以及长时间等候的情况有多少。也请记住，仅凭这三个人的记录，不能保证下一位顾客的等候时间。

items.script: Commentator: Let’s follow a day in a fictional village with a communal drying area. Each clothesline has a small wooden tag. Even when there is no laundry visible on a line, residents do not immediately hang their own clothes there. They first look at which side of the tag is showing. The circle side means someone else may use it, and the diagonal-line side means the user has stepped away temporarily. Residents agreed on this so people can keep their place while taking dry laundry inside and bringing out the next load. The tag itself cannot physically block the line. The agreement works only if newcomers are taught the symbols’ meanings and users turn the tag back to the circle side when they finish. For a broken clothesline, residents tie a cord across it instead of using the wooden tag. Being available, being temporarily unattended, and being unusable are different states. Small, simple signs let people coordinate their next actions without meeting to explain.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 공동 건조장을 운영하는 가상 마을의 하루를 따라가 보겠습니다. 이곳에는 빨랫줄마다 작은 나무패가 하나씩 달려 있습니다. 빨랫감이 보이지 않는 줄 앞에서도 주민은 곧바로 자기 빨래를 걸지 않습니다. 나무패의 면을 먼저 살핍니다. 동그라미 면은 다른 사람이 써도 된다는 뜻이고, 빗금 면은 사용자가 잠시 자리를 비웠다는 뜻입니다. 다 마른 빨래를 들여놓고 다음 빨래를 가져오는 동안에도 자리를 유지할 수 있도록 주민들이 정한 약속입니다. 나무패 자체가 줄을 막아 주지는 못합니다. 새로 온 사람에게 표시의 뜻을 알려 주고, 사용을 끝낸 사람이 동그라미 면으로 돌려놓아야 이 약속이 작동합니다. 주민들은 고장 난 줄에는 나무패 대신 끈을 가로질러 묶습니다. 비어 있음, 잠시 비움, 쓸 수 없음이 서로 다른 상태이기 때문입니다. 작고 단순한 표시는 서로 만나 설명하지 않아도 다음 행동을 조정하게 합니다.

items.script: Lecturer: In work with several connected stages, do not assume that the sum of the time spent at each stage is the interval between completed items in continuous production. Consider a hypothetical stage-prop production process. Making the frame of one prop takes three minutes, drying its surface takes six minutes, and packaging takes three minutes. Each stage handles one item at a time, but different stages can work on different props simultaneously. The first item takes twelve minutes to finish. However, when work keeps arriving and the drying stage runs without a break, one finished item comes out every six minutes. The stages before and after drying can keep going only as the middle drying stage becomes able to accept the next prop. Reducing frame-making time to one minute does not mean a finished item comes out every minute. It may instead lead to a buildup of frames waiting to dry. To shorten the overall production interval, we need to identify which stage limits the flow. One person’s speed and the speed of the whole workflow are different matters.

items.script:
Host: You made a scale model of the stage for the new theater. Looking down from above, you can see at a glance where everything is. Do you use it to judge whether the audience can see well too?
Model maker: From above, we can check the placement of the set pieces, but that does not represent the audience’s view. For example, a prop behind a table may be visible from above but hidden from someone seated lower down. So we put a small camera at an audience-seat position and look at the model.
Host: As long as the stage is scaled correctly, can you put the camera at any convenient height?
Model maker: The viewing position must be scaled by the same proportion too. This model is one-tenth of the actual size. If we assume an audience eye level of 120 centimeters above the real floor, we place the lens 12 centimeters above the model floor. We also check from positions in the front and back rows and on both sides, so we do not generalize the result from one seat to the entire audience area.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 새 공연장 무대의 축소 모형을 만드셨는데, 위에서 내려다보면 어디에 무엇이 놓였는지 한눈에 보입니다. 이걸로 객석에서도 잘 보일지 판단하시나요?

items.script:
主持人: 您做了新剧场舞台的缩尺模型，从上往下看，哪里放着什么一目了然。您也用这个判断观众席能否看清吗？

Host: You made a scale model of the stage for the new theater. Looking down from above, you can see at a glance where everything is. Do you use it to judge whether the audience can see well too?
Model maker: From above, we can check the placement of the set pieces, but that does not represent the audience’s view. For example, a prop behind a table may be visible from above but hidden from someone seated lower down. So we put a small camera at an audience-seat position and look at the model.
Host: As long as the stage is scaled correctly, can you put the camera at any convenient height?
Model maker: The viewing position must be scaled by the same proportion too. This model is one-tenth of the actual size. If we assume an audience eye level of 120 centimeters above the real floor, we place the lens 12 centimeters above the model floor. We also check from positions in the front and back rows and on both sides, so we do not generalize the result from one seat to the entire audience area.

items.script: Lecturer: Let’s consider a budget decision for a hypothetical event. Suppose advertising has already been paid for during preparation and the money cannot be refunded even if the event is canceled. Later, when expected attendance falls, someone says, “It would be a waste of that money, so we should go ahead.” But continuing involves additional costs and generates new income. Canceling removes both those additional costs and that income. To compare the financial outcomes from now on, we need to examine the amounts that differ between the two choices. The advertising payment will not come back under either choice, so its size alone does not make continuing more favorable. A deposit paid in advance but refundable upon cancellation is different, however. That money must be included in the comparison because today’s choice changes how much remains. Of course, the event’s cultural value and the matter of keeping commitments are separate considerations. Excluding past spending from today’s comparison also does not mean there is no need to assess who decided on that spending and why.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 가상 행사의 예산 결정을 생각해 보겠습니다. 행사를 준비하며 이미 홍보비를 냈고, 이 돈은 취소해도 돌려받을 수 없다고 합시다. 이후 예상 관객이 줄자 누군가 말합니다. “그 돈이 아까우니 행사를 계속해야 한다.” 하지만 계속하면 추가 비용이 들고 새 수입도 생깁니다. 취소하면 이 추가 비용과 수입은 모두 없어집니다. 앞으로의 재정 결과를 비교하려면 두 선택에서 달라지는 금액을 보아야 합니다. 이미 낸 홍보비는 어느 선택에서도 돌아오지 않으므로, 그 금액이 크다는 이유만으로 계속하는 편이 유리해지지는 않습니다. 반면 미리 낸 돈이라도 취소하면 환급받을 수 있는 보증금은 다릅니다. 그 돈은 오늘의 선택에 따라 남는 금액이 달라지므로 비교에 포함해야 합니다. 물론 행사의 문화적 가치나 약속을 지키는 문제는 별도의 판단 요소입니다. 또한 과거 지출을 오늘의 비교에서 빼는 것은 그 지출을 누가 왜 결정했는지 평가할 필요가 없다는 뜻도 아닙니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 我们来考虑一个假设活动的预算决定。假设筹备活动时已经付了宣传费，即使取消活动也不能退回。之后预计观众减少，有人说：“那笔钱太可惜了，活动应该继续。”但继续举办会产生额外费用，也会带来新的收入。取消则这两项额外费用和收入都不会发生。比较今后的财务结果时，应看两种选择之间会改变的金额。已经支付的宣传费无论选哪种都拿不回来，所以不能只因金额大，就认为继续举办更有利。相反，即使已预付，取消时可以退回的保证金也不同。它会因今天的选择而改变剩余金额，因此应纳入比较。当然，活动的文化价值和履行承诺的问题是另外的判断因素。此外，把过去支出从今天的比较中排除，也不表示不需要评估是谁、为什么决定了那笔支出。

items.script:
Planner: Many visitors want to take photographs, while others find it inconvenient when cameras block their view of the artworks. Instead of always allowing photography or banning it entirely, how about dividing the time?
Visitor: If we only get a short time to look after the photography period, wouldn’t it be difficult to appreciate the works calmly?
Planner: We plan to make the first forty minutes of each hour a period for viewing without photography, followed by twenty minutes when photography is also allowed. We will announce the timetable before visitors buy tickets so they can choose when to enter.
Visitor: In that case, it seems worth trying. However, please also check actual visitors’ reactions to see whether they can view the works sufficiently during the period without photography.

策划人员: 很多观众想留下照片，也有观众觉得相机挡在作品前面很不方便。与其一直允许拍摄或全面禁止，不如划分时间，怎么样？
观众: 如果拍摄时间之后只能看一小会儿，不就难以静心欣赏了吗？

items.script:
Host: In this game, players originally chose action cards in turn. Have you now changed it so they choose, place the cards face down, and reveal them all at once?
Game designer: Previously, someone choosing later could see the earlier player’s card and then change their own choice. It was hard to say they had decided under the same conditions. Now we reveal the cards after everyone has finished choosing, so players cannot revise their choices after seeing someone else’s answer.
Host: Then is the aim to produce similar scores even when players differ in skill?
Game designer: No. Remembering what an opponent chose in the previous turn and predicting their next action are still important strategies. What we removed is the opportunity to see someone else’s choice for the current turn in advance and revise your own simply because you reveal later.

游戏设计者: 以前后选的人能先看前面玩家的卡，再改变自己的选择，很难说是在同样条件下决定的。现在等所有人选好之后再公开，就不能看了别人的答案再修改了。
主持人: 也就是说，即使玩家水平不同，也要让分数差不多吗？
游戏设计者: 不是。记住对手上一轮选了什么，并预测下一步行动，这样的策略仍然重要。我们取消的，只是由于自己较晚公开，就能提前看见对手本轮选择并据此修改的机会。

transcriptTurns.textKo: 이 게임은 원래 차례대로 행동 카드를 골랐는데 이제는 골라서 뒤집어 놓았다가 한꺼번에 공개하는 방식으로 바꾸셨습니까?
transcriptTurns.speaker: 主持人
transcriptTurns.text: 这个游戏原来是依次选择行动卡，现在改成选好后反扣着放，最后同时公开了吗？

transcriptTurns.textKo: 예전에는 뒤에 고르는 사람이 앞사람 카드를 본 뒤 자기 선택을 바꿀 수 있었습니다. 같은 조건에서 결정했다고 보기 어려웠습니다. 지금은 모두 선택을 마친 다음에 공개하므로 다른 사람의 답을 보고 고칠 수 없습니다.
transcriptTurns.speaker: 游戏设计者
transcriptTurns.text: 以前后选的人能先看前面玩家的卡，再改变自己的选择，很难说是在同样条件下决定的。现在等所有人选好之后再公开，就不能看了别人的答案再修改了。

transcriptTurns.textKo: 그러면 사람마다 실력이 달라도 비슷한 점수가 나오도록 한 것입니까?

transcriptTurns.text: 也就是说，即使玩家水平不同，也要让分数差不多吗？

transcriptTurns.textKo: 그렇지는 않습니다. 이전 차례에서 상대가 어떤 선택을 했는지 기억하고 다음 행동을 예상하는 전략은 여전히 중요합니다. 없앤 것은 나중에 공개한다는 이유만으로 이번 선택을 미리 보고 수정하는 기회입니다.

items.script:
Proponent: There are three project proposals, 가, 나 and 다, so we can first put two to a vote, then compare the winner with the remaining proposal. It is a simple method of choosing whichever of the two receives more votes.
Reviewer: But in this preference survey, 가 beat 나, 나 beat 다, and 다 beat 가. Even if people’s preferences stay the same, the proposal left at the end changes depending on which two are matched first.
Proponent: If the problem is someone choosing an advantageous order, how about drawing lots to decide the order before we begin?
Reviewer: That could reduce the scope for deliberately manipulating the order. However, drawing lots does not remove the effect the order has on the result. When explaining the final choice, we should also disclose the procedure used to decide it.

items.script: Lecturer: In some surveys, measurements are rounded to the nearest ten before publication to avoid displaying detailed figures. Suppose this survey displays all values from forty-five through fifty-four as fifty. Records originally measuring forty-seven and fifty-two then become indistinguishable in the published table. Even if you know the rounding method exactly, the published fifty alone cannot identify one particular original number. When displayed, several different values were merged into one; when working backward, the information identifying which one it was is missing. Therefore, if detailed comparisons will be needed later, the original measurements should be kept separately from the published table. This is not a matter of an incorrect rounding calculation, but of how much information was retained in the records.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 어떤 조사에서는 세부 숫자를 보이지 않으려고 측정값을 십 단위로 반올림해 공개합니다. 이 조사에서는 사십오부터 오십사까지를 모두 오십으로 표시한다고 합시다. 원래 사십칠이었던 자료와 오십이였던 자료가 공개 표에서는 구별되지 않는 것입니다. 반올림 방법을 정확히 알더라도 공개된 오십만 보고 어느 수였는지 하나로 정할 수는 없습니다. 표시할 때는 여러 다른 값이 하나로 모였는데, 거꾸로 갈 때는 그중 무엇이었는지 알려 줄 정보가 사라졌기 때문입니다. 따라서 나중에 세부 비교를 해야 한다면, 공개 표와 별도로 원래 측정값을 보관할 필요가 있습니다. 이는 반올림 계산을 잘못했다는 문제가 아니라 기록을 얼마나 남겼느냐의 문제입니다.

items.script:
Reporter: I’m at a noise inspection in the new exhibition room. I can see two different numbers on the meter’s display. What is the difference?
Person in charge: The upper number is the level of the sound being heard now. The lower number is the highest value since this measurement began, and it changes only when a louder sound occurs. Even after a brief sound such as a door slamming has passed, that record remains.
Reporter: The top currently shows forty and the bottom seventy-five. Does that mean it was seventy-five throughout the measurement?
Person in charge: No. It means a sound of that level occurred during the measurement interval; this maximum alone does not tell us how long it lasted. When we measure another room, we clear the previous room’s maximum and start a new interval. That keeps it from being mixed with the current room’s record.

记者: 我现在在新展厅的噪声检查现场。仪器屏幕上有两个不同的数字，它们有什么区别？

负责人: 上面的数字是现在听到的声音大小。下面是这次测量开始以来的最大值，只有出现更大的声音时才会改变。即使用力关门时的短促声响已经过去，记录也会保留下来。
记者: 现在上面显示四十，下面显示七十五。可以理解为整个测量期间一直是七十五吗？
负责人: 不可以。这表示测量区间内出现过那样大小的声音，仅凭最高值并不能知道持续了多久。测量另一个房间时，我们会清除前一个房间的最高值，再开始新的测量区间。这样才不会与当前房间的记录混在一起。

items.script:
Host: I’d like to ask about a puzzle in which a board of alternating black and white squares is filled with two-square covering pieces. Do you need to move the pieces around many times to solve it?
Researcher: In some cases, we can tell that it is impossible without even placing them. Each piece covers only two squares that share an edge, so however you rotate it, it covers one black square and one white square.
Host: The board now has eight black squares and six white squares remaining.
Researcher: Then pieces covering equal numbers of the two colors cannot fill the entire board. That remains true even if the total number of squares is even. Conversely, if the two colors have equal numbers, this reason alone cannot establish impossibility, but it cannot establish that completion is possible either. We must also check whether separated squares prevent pieces from being placed.

items.script:
主持人: 想请教一个拼板问题：在黑白格交替排列的板上，用每块覆盖两格的盖板填满。是不是必须反复挪动盖板才能解开？
研究人员: 有些情况下，不用实际摆放就能知道不可能完成。每块盖板只能覆盖两格共边的格子，所以无论怎样旋转，都只覆盖一格黑色和一格白色。
主持人: 现在板上剩下八格黑色、六格白色。
研究人员: 那么，每次覆盖两种颜色相同数量的盖板，就不可能填满整个板。即使总格数是偶数也一样。反过来，如果两种颜色数量相等，虽然不能仅凭这个理由断定不可能，却也不能断定一定能完成。还要检查是否存在分离的格子，导致盖板无法放置。

items.script: Lecturer: There are three red balls and two blue balls of the same shape in a box. Before drawing a ball, suppose we mix them well so that every ball is equally likely to be selected. If we draw one, look at its color and put it back, the contents of the box will be the same as before for the next draw. Several red draws do not mean that a blue ball must come next. But things change if we set aside the ball we have drawn. If we remove one red ball without putting it back, two balls of each color remain in the box. We cannot determine the next result, but we can say that the conditions for the next selection have changed. To judge whether a previous result has an effect, we must look not only at the sequence of results but also at what the contents of the box became afterward.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 같은 모양의 빨간 공 세 개와 파란 공 두 개가 상자에 있습니다. 공을 뽑기 전에 잘 섞어서 어느 공이나 뽑힐 가능성이 같다고 합시다. 하나를 뽑아 색을 보고 다시 넣으면 다음에도 상자 안의 구성은 처음과 같습니다. 빨간 공이 여러 번 나왔다고 해서 다음에는 파란 공이 나와야 하는 것은 아닙니다. 반면 뽑은 공을 따로 빼 두면 이야기가 달라집니다. 빨간 공을 하나 빼고 돌려놓지 않았다면 상자에는 두 색이 두 개씩 남습니다. 다음 결과를 확정할 수는 없지만, 다음 선택의 조건이 바뀌었다고 말할 수는 있습니다. 앞의 결과가 영향을 주는지 판단하려면 나온 결과의 순서만 볼 것이 아니라 그 뒤에 상자 안의 구성이 어떻게 되었는지를 봐야 합니다.

items.script:
Narrator: At this village restaurant, meal vouchers that people buy and those provided through assistance look the same. They used to have different colors, but now even the paper and printing are identical.
Staff member: We did not want a diner’s presentation of a voucher to reveal to people nearby how the diner had received it. We do not have separate queues for accepting them either. Eligibility for assistance is checked at an earlier stage, before the voucher is given out; the restaurant simply accepts the voucher.
Narrator: Even though the vouchers look the same, the numbers sold and provided through assistance are recorded separately when they are issued. Visible distinctions have been reduced, but distinctions needed for internal accounting have not been removed. The restaurant focused less on the circumstances that brought people there than on their sharing a place to eat a meal.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose the time of a task that three people must start together has changed. The coordinator sends each of them a text message, and all three read it. Each person now knows the new time but may not know whether the other two know it as well. If each person replies to the coordinator, the coordinator learns that all three have confirmed it. But if only the coordinator who received those replies knows this, the participants may remain worried. So this team decided that each person would leave a confirmation mark on a board they can all see and read the other two people’s marks before starting work. The purpose of this method is not to send more copies of the same information. It is to let people mutually confirm not only their own readiness but also the readiness of those they will work with. If the marks are made automatically or someone else confirms on a person’s behalf, it is difficult to say this purpose has been achieved.

items.script:
Host: This household-goods competition announced that entries would be judged on ease of use and quality of execution. But after seeing the submissions, designing with less material also seems important. Would adding points for that now help us choose better work?
Judge: That criterion is worth considering. However, participants have spent time and materials according to the announced standards. Adding a criterion after submissions are complete could disadvantage people who would have made their entries differently had they known the new standard.
Host: Does that mean we must keep using the same standards even if they are inadequate?
Judge: We should judge this round’s entries as originally announced, while addressing the limitations we found when preparing the next competition. Announcing the points allocation as well as any new criteria before applications lets participants decide what to take into account. We need to distinguish the timing of improving standards from that of applying those standards to people who have already entered.

主持人: 这次日用品设计征集比赛公布的评价标准是使用便利性与完成质量。可是看到参赛作品后，减少材料用量的设计似乎也很重要。现在增加这一项的分值，不是能选出更好的作品吗？
评审: 这一项值得考虑。不过，参赛者已经按照公布的标准投入了时间和材料。提交结束后再增加标准，可能对那些若事先知道新标准就会采用不同制作方式的人不利。
主持人: 那么，即使标准不够完善，也得一直照旧使用吗？
评审: 本次作品应按最初公布的标准评审，但发现的局限应在准备下次征集时加以改进。把新项目和分值安排都在报名之前公布，参赛者才能决定需要考虑什么。修改标准与把该标准用于已经参赛的人，需要区分适用时间。

items.script:
Host: This household-goods competition announced that entries would be judged on ease of use and quality of execution. But after seeing the submissions, designing with less material also seems important. Would adding points for that now help us choose better work?
Judge: That criterion is worth considering. However, participants have spent time and materials according to the announced standards. Adding a criterion after submissions are complete could disadvantage people who would have made their entries differently had they known the new standard.
Host: Does that mean we must keep using the same standards even if they are inadequate?
Judge: We should judge this round’s entries as originally announced, while addressing the limitations we found when preparing the next competition. Announcing the points allocation as well as any new criteria before applications lets participants decide what to take into account. We need to distinguish the timing of improving standards from that of applying those standards to people who have already entered.

items.script: Lecturer: Let us test a rule using cards with a color on one side and a number on the other. The rule is that if a card is blue, the number on its other side is even. Four cards show blue, red, four and seven, respectively. If the back of the blue card has an odd number, that violates the rule, so we need to turn that card over. We must also check the card showing seven, because a blue back would be the same violation. In contrast, a red back on the card showing the even number four would not violate the rule. That is because the rule did not say that an even number implies blue. The red card likewise has no restriction on its number. Finding more examples that fit a rule is different from checking places where the rule could fail. We first need to decide what would actually count as a violation so that we do not miss a necessary check.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 한쪽에는 색, 반대쪽에는 숫자가 있는 카드로 규칙을 검사해 보겠습니다. 규칙은 파란 카드라면 반대쪽 숫자가 짝수라는 것입니다. 파란색, 빨간색, 사, 칠이 각각 보이는 카드 네 장이 있습니다. 파란 카드의 뒷면이 홀수라면 규칙 위반이니 그 카드는 뒤집어 봐야 합니다. 칠이 보이는 카드도 뒤가 파란색이면 같은 위반이므로 확인해야 합니다. 반면 짝수 사의 뒤가 빨간색이라고 해도 규칙을 어기지 않습니다. 규칙은 짝수라면 파란색이라고 말하지 않았기 때문입니다. 빨간 카드 역시 숫자에 대한 제한이 없습니다. 규칙에 맞는 예를 더 찾는 것과, 규칙이 틀릴 가능성이 있는 곳을 검사하는 것은 다릅니다. 어떤 경우가 실제 위반인지 먼저 정해야 필요한 확인을 빠뜨리지 않습니다.

Staff member: If you only remove an item, we keep counting from the time you first left the bag. You aren’t ending the storage service. Under that arrangement, would you like to keep the bag stored and retrieve only the laptop?

items.script:
Host: I understand this play began with your workplace experiences. Is the main character’s colleague someone you actually know?
Writer: I haven’t reproduced one person exactly. I combined one colleague’s words and another colleague’s choices in a single character. I also brought events from different times into conflict within the same scene.
Host: Why did you structure it that way even though it differs from what actually happened?
Writer: Introducing every individual on stage can obscure the conflict I really want to show. By following one character’s choices, I wanted to reveal where different expectations collide. However, I stated in the program that I had reworked several experiences.
Host: So even if one action by a character resembles something a real colleague did, we can’t attribute all of that character’s other actions to that person?
Writer: That’s right. It begins with experience, but it isn’t a record proving the actions of one real person.

主持人: 听说这部戏源自您的工作经历。主人公的同事是您实际认识的人吗？
作家: 并不是原样照搬某一个人。我把一个同事说过的话和另一个同事的选择，集中到同一个角色身上；还把不同时期发生的事放到同一场景里产生碰撞。
主持人: 即使与实际情况不同，也这样安排，有什么原因吗？
作家: 在舞台上逐一介绍很多人物，会让真正想展示的冲突变得模糊。我想让观众跟随一个角色的选择，看清不同期待在哪里发生冲突。不过，节目册上说明了这是对多段经历的重新编排。

items.script:
Planner: When we let people speak in the order they raise their hands, it’s always much the same people who speak first. At the next meeting, how about giving everyone a turn, just for the opening round?
Resident: It feels burdensome if my turn comes before I’ve organized my thoughts. Some people may only want to listen.
Planner: In that case, you can pass without giving a reason. After the opening round, we’ll speak freely as we do now, and you may share ideas that come to you then. The aim isn’t to make people speak, but to offer an opening to those who find it hard to join in.
Resident: If we can pass and speak later, it seems worth trying. But I’d like us to see whether the people who used to be quiet actually find participating more comfortable.

Host: In this translation, the same character’s way of speaking changes partway through. Wouldn’t it be better to keep one character’s speech consistent?
Translator: In the original, too, two people speak with some distance when they first meet, then grow closer through shared events. If I translate only word meanings and make every line equally polite, that change disappears.
Host: Are you saying there are limits to assigning one translated expression to each honorific expression in the original?
Translator: Yes, because languages express interpersonal distance differently. I can adjust sentence endings or forms of address without adding or removing events from the original. I don’t stop at checking whether one sentence sounds natural. I read earlier and later scenes side by side to check whether the development in the relationship remains.

items.script:
Team leader: Everyone used the studio for the same amount of time for this shoot. It would be simple to settle the bill by adding the rental and printing fees and dividing by the number of people.
Team member: I agree with sharing the rental fee. But each person chose as many prints as they wanted. Someone who ordered no prints and someone who ordered many shouldn’t pay the same printing fee as well.
Team leader: I understand the distinction, but wouldn’t it become more complicated if we had to rely on memory afterward to know who chose how many?
Team member: We can record each person’s chosen quantity and cost when they order the prints. We can make those details available for that person to check too. I don’t mean changing the way we divide the rental fee.
Team leader: If we have records to verify individual orders, we’ll split it that way. I’ll show the shared expenses and the amounts chosen by individuals separately.

组长: 这次拍摄，大家使用摄影棚的时间都一样。把租用费和照片冲印费相加，再按人数平分，结算会比较简单。

组长: 我理解区分的意思，可事后只靠记忆回想谁选了几张，不会更复杂吗？

组长: 如果有记录可以核对个人订单，那就这样分。我会把共同使用的费用与个人选择的费用分开说明。

items.script:
Reporter: I hear this community bus has introduced a policy of waiting briefly for passengers transferring from city buses. When does it wait?
Staff member: First, we must receive notice that there are passengers who need to transfer. We wait only when the city bus is confirmed as expected to arrive within five minutes of our scheduled departure. If its expected arrival is more than five minutes later, we leave at the original time.
Reporter: If the policy is meant to help transferring passengers, why put a limit on waiting?
Staff member: We want to help people who would face a long wait for the next bus if they missed this one. But arrival times also matter to those already aboard. So we accept only a short delay when there is an actual transfer need. Even if we have decided to wait, we leave once five minutes have passed since the scheduled departure time.
Reporter: It is now the scheduled departure time, and we have notice that a city bus carrying transferring passengers will arrive in three minutes.
Staff member: We wait in this case. But even if that bus is later than expected, we won’t extend the established limit.

items.script:
Reporter: I hear this community bus has introduced a policy of waiting briefly for passengers transferring from city buses. When does it wait?
Staff member: First, we must receive notice that there are passengers who need to transfer. We wait only when the city bus is confirmed as expected to arrive within five minutes of our scheduled departure. If its expected arrival is more than five minutes later, we leave at the original time.
Reporter: If the policy is meant to help transferring passengers, why put a limit on waiting?
Staff member: We want to help people who would face a long wait for the next bus if they missed this one. But arrival times also matter to those already aboard. So we accept only a short delay when there is an actual transfer need. Even if we have decided to wait, we leave once five minutes have passed since the scheduled departure time.
Reporter: It is now the scheduled departure time, and we have notice that a city bus carrying transferring passengers will arrive in three minutes.
Staff member: We wait in this case. But even if that bus is later than expected, we won’t extend the established limit.

items.script:
Host: I prepare a list of questions before an interview, but unexpected answers disrupt the order. Isn’t it safer to read through the list to the end?
Speaker: A list helps ensure that essential topics aren’t missed. But if someone has just begun explaining an important reason and you move to the next question, you miss the meaning of what they said. Keep the prepared topics in mind while being able to follow a new question arising from an answer for a while.
Host: For example, what if someone talking about closing their shop says it wasn’t because business was bad, but because of another choice?
Speaker: Then it’s better to ask what that choice was rather than jump straight to the next listed question about preparing to open the shop. Nor should you decide on their behalf, before hearing the answer, that it must have been because of family. After clarifying that story, you can continue with the key topics you planned in the remaining time.

items.script: Speaker: Today, let’s judge only what a sentence explicitly states, without other contextual information. Consider the sentence “Not all the students submitted the assignment.” Changing this to “Nobody submitted it” makes a stronger claim than the original. What the original establishes is that at least one student did not submit it. That sentence alone does not determine who submitted it or how many did. It rules out neither the case where nobody submitted it nor a case where some did. So adding that exactly one person failed to submit, or that there must also be students who submitted, introduces unverified information. When summarizing similar sentences, too, retain only what can be stated with certainty rather than filling gaps with an imagined plausible situation.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 오늘은 다른 상황 정보 없이 문장에 명시된 내용만 판단해 보겠습니다. 학생들이 모두 과제를 제출한 것은 아니라는 문장을 보십시오. 이것을 아무도 제출하지 않았다고 바꾸면 원문보다 강한 말이 됩니다. 원문에서 확실한 것은 제출하지 않은 학생이 적어도 한 명 있다는 점입니다. 누가 제출했고 몇 명이 제출했는지는 그 문장만으로 정해지지 않습니다. 실제로 아무도 내지 않은 경우도 배제되지 않고, 몇 명은 낸 경우도 배제되지 않습니다. 따라서 정확히 한 명이 안 냈다거나 제출한 학생도 반드시 있다고 덧붙이면 확인하지 않은 정보를 넣게 됩니다. 비슷한 문장을 요약할 때도 그럴듯한 상황을 상상해 채우기보다, 확실히 말할 수 있는 범위만 남겨야 합니다.

items.script:
Commentator: The records team is reading old film and converting it into computer files. This process is called scanning. In the photograph file just created, a small dot is visible that cannot immediately be identified as part of the original scene or a mark introduced during conversion.
Researcher: We could remove the dots all at once to make the image look smooth. But that could also erase a pattern on clothing at the time of the photograph, so we first enlarge and compare the original film. Today, one dot was absent from the film. After we cleaned the scanner glass and read the film again, that dot disappeared from the file as well. Another dot was visible on the clothing in the film and remained after rescanning.
Commentator: So rather than treating a small dot based only on its appearance, you examine the stage at which it was introduced?
Researcher: Exactly. Our purpose is not to redesign the scene in the photograph. We correct marks added during conversion, but we do not remove original information merely because we dislike its appearance. If comparison still does not establish a dot’s origin, we document its state and leave it in place.

items.script: Speaker: On the surface, “The door is open” is a sentence reporting a state. But if someone who has stopped a conversation because of noise outside says it while looking at a colleague next to the door, it may be a request to close it. Conversely, if someone enters a stuffy room and says it happily because air is circulating, it is hard to understand it as asking for the door to be closed. The sentence form is the same, but the problem to address and the action the listener can take differ. This does not mean that context lets us assign meanings however we like. We need evidence about what discomfort was mentioned and whom the remark addressed. For example, if a presenter in an air-conditioned meeting room tells a staff member beside the temperature control that it is cold enough to make their hands feel chilled, the staff member can consider whether this is a simple temperature report or a request for an adjustment. If it is unclear, checking by asking “Would you like me to reduce the airflow?” is more appropriate than dismissing it because no request was made or changing other settings all at once.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 문이 열려 있네요라는 말은 겉으로 보면 상태를 알리는 문장입니다. 그러나 문밖 소음 때문에 대화를 멈춘 사람이 문 옆에 있는 동료를 보며 말했다면 닫아 달라는 부탁일 수 있습니다. 반대로 답답한 방에 들어와 바람이 통한다며 반갑게 말했다면 닫으라는 뜻으로 듣기 어렵습니다. 문장 형태가 같아도 해결하려는 문제와 상대가 할 수 있는 행동이 다르기 때문입니다. 그렇다고 상황만 보고 뜻을 마음대로 정해도 된다는 말은 아닙니다. 어떤 불편을 말했고 누구에게 말했는지 근거를 모아야 합니다. 예를 들어 냉방 중인 회의실에서 발표자가 온도 조절기 옆 직원에게 손이 시릴 정도로 춥다고 말했다면, 직원은 단순한 온도 보고인지 조절 요청인지 생각할 수 있습니다. 분명하지 않다면 바람을 약하게 해 드릴까요라고 확인하는 것이, 요청은 없었다며 넘기거나 다른 설정까지 한꺼번에 바꾸는 것보다 적절합니다.

items.script: 演讲者: “门开着呢”从表面上看，是报告状态的句子。但如果一个人因门外噪声而停下谈话，看着门边的同事这样说，就可能是在请对方关门。反过来，如果走进令人感觉憋闷的房间，因为有风流通而高兴地这样说，就很难理解成让人关门。句子形式虽然相同，要解决的问题和对方能采取的行动却不同。但这并不意味着只凭情境就能任意确定含义。需要收集依据，看看说了什么不适，又是对谁说的。例如，在开着空调的会议室里，报告者对温度调节器旁的工作人员说，冷得手都发凉，工作人员可以考虑这是单纯报告温度，还是请求调节。如果不明确，问一句“需要把风调小一些吗？”来确认，比以没有提出请求为由略过，或一次改动其他设置，更为恰当。
