items.script:
Host: I understand sponsorship is needed to distribute the local newsletter free of charge. Can you apply the same standards when writing about a sponsoring organization?
Editor: We disclose who supports us. But displaying a sponsorship notice does not in itself permit interference with the content. We must distinguish the support that makes the newsletter possible from decisions about what goes into an article.
Host: Do you reject every request from a sponsor to revise an article?
Editor: No. If we have printed an event date incorrectly and they provide verification, we should correct it. But asking us to remove a verified inconvenient fact because it harms the organization’s image is different. What matters is not so much whether the person pointing it out provided funding, but what evidence supports the change and what content they want changed.
Host: So you uphold both sponsorship disclosure and fact-checking, while judging revision requests on their substance?
Editor: Exactly. Neither unconditional obedience because we received support nor rejection of every criticism in the name of independence is our principle.

items.script: Speaker: A claim appearing in a text does not by itself show that the author accepts it. Authors may quote a claim to introduce their own view, but they may also quote it to present what they intend to criticize. Rather than isolating the sentence inside quotation marks, examine who said it and how the author evaluates it before and after the quotation. Here is a short example. An organizer said that the more notices there are, the easier things become for users. But amid notices repeating the same warnings many times, it was difficult to find the actual registration location. What is needed now is not more information notices, but an ordering of the information users need to find. If we summarize the first claim as the conclusion of the whole text, we reverse the author’s stance, which is to explain that claim’s limitations later. On the other hand, saying the claim never appeared in the text is also wrong. We must distinguish the fact that it was quoted from the judgment that it was endorsed.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 글에 어떤 주장이 실려 있다는 사실만으로 글쓴이가 그 주장을 받아들였다고 볼 수는 없습니다. 자신의 의견을 소개하려고 인용할 수도 있지만, 비판할 대상을 먼저 보여 주려고 인용할 수도 있기 때문입니다. 따옴표 안의 문장만 떼어 읽지 말고 누가 한 말인지, 앞뒤에서 글쓴이가 그것을 어떻게 평가하는지 보아야 합니다. 다음 짧은 예를 들어 보겠습니다. 어떤 운영자는 안내 문구가 많을수록 이용자는 더 편해진다고 말했다. 그러나 같은 주의를 여러 번 반복한 게시물 사이에서 정작 접수 장소를 찾기 어려웠다. 이제 필요한 것은 안내의 양을 늘리는 일이 아니라 이용자가 찾을 정보의 순서를 세우는 일이다. 여기서 처음 나온 주장을 글 전체의 결론으로 요약하면, 뒤에서 그 주장의 한계를 설명한 글쓴이의 태도를 거꾸로 옮기게 됩니다. 반대로 그 주장이 글에 없었다고 해도 틀립니다. 인용되었다는 사실과 지지받았다는 판단을 나누어 읽어야 합니다.

Host: This is a song everyone knows, but its mood has changed quite a lot. Did you start by creating a new melody?
Arranger: At first, I changed the melody a lot too. But a colleague who listened said they couldn’t tell what song it was. I wasn’t trying to create an unfamiliar new piece. I wanted people to discover a different feeling in a familiar song.

Arranger: I reduced the changes to the melody and changed the accompaniment’s rhythm and arrangement of instruments. Because a melody people could sing along to remained, listeners could also sense what had changed. In effect, I considered both making the original recognizable and creating a new mood.

items.script:
Host: This park has benches facing each other as well as benches facing the river side by side. Wouldn’t it look tidier to align them in one direction?

items.script:
Panelist A: That character in yesterday’s drama was so irritating. So I wrote that the actor was bad at acting.
Panelist B: You can certainly feel angry at a character’s behavior. But disliking the character alone makes it difficult to judge how the actor delivered the lines or facial expressions.
Panelist A: Then should I say the acting was good because it made the audience angry?
Panelist B: You can’t immediately jump to that opposite conclusion either. The story’s setup may have made you angry. You can still express your dislike, but when evaluating the acting, you need to examine separately whether the voice and movements suited the scene.

Panelist A: That character in yesterday’s drama was so irritating. So I wrote that the actor was bad at acting.
Panelist B: You can certainly feel angry at a character’s behavior. But disliking the character alone makes it difficult to judge how the actor delivered the lines or facial expressions.
Panelist A: Then should I say the acting was good because it made the audience angry?
Panelist B: You can’t immediately jump to that opposite conclusion either. The story’s setup may have made you angry. You can still express your dislike, but when evaluating the acting, you need to examine separately whether the voice and movements suited the scene.

items.script: Lecturer: Two people looked at the same clock and confirmed that it was three p.m. One had to finish work by four but said that less than half was done and that it was already three. The other was waiting for a train departing at four and said it was still only three. Their different expressions do not mean that one of them read the time incorrectly. The first felt that time had passed quickly because there was a lot of work left, while the second felt there was still time to wait before departure. To understand 벌써, “already,” and 아직, “still,” checking the time alone is not enough. We must also consider what the speaker was waiting for or trying to finish, and how much waiting or work was involved.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 두 사람이 같은 시계를 보고 오후 세 시임을 확인했습니다. 한 사람은 네 시까지 일을 마쳐야 하는데 절반도 못 했다며 벌써 세 시라고 했습니다. 다른 사람은 네 시에 출발하는 기차를 기다리며 아직 세 시라고 했습니다. 두 표현이 다르다고 한쪽이 시간을 잘못 본 것은 아닙니다. 첫 사람은 남은 일이 많아 시간이 빨리 갔다고 느끼고, 둘째 사람은 출발까지 기다릴 시간이 남았다고 느낀 것입니다. 벌써와 아직을 이해하려면 시각만 확인해서는 부족합니다. 말하는 사람이 무엇을 얼마나 기다리거나 마치려 했는지도 함께 봐야 합니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 两个人看着同一只钟，确认是下午三点。一人最晚要在四点完成工作，却连一半都没做完，于是说已经三点了。另一个人等着四点出发的火车，说才三点。两种表达不同，并不意味着其中一人看错了时间。前者因为剩下的工作多，觉得时间过得快；后者则觉得离出发还有一段时间要等。要理解“벌써”和“아직”，只确认时刻还不够。还要看说话者在等待什么、要完成什么，以及所涉及的等待或任务有多少。

items.script:
Woman: When I presented the event budget proposal earlier, someone asked, “Does that amount include labor costs?” I thought they were against the proposal.
Man: Think about what they said afterward too. When told those costs were included, they replied, “Under those conditions, it should be feasible.”
Woman: So they needed to know whether there would be additional costs before they could judge.
Man: Exactly. A question doesn’t always mean agreement, but in this case they made a judgment after checking what the amount covered. Rather than deciding it was opposition based on a single question, it would be better to consider the response that followed too.

items.script: Commentator: A visitor thought that the three clocks in the exhibition room were accurate because they all showed the same time. But the inspection records showed that a staff member had set all three by the clock in the information office. That clock was five minutes ahead of the actual time. So the agreement among the three exhibition-room clocks shows only that they followed the same reference; it does not guarantee that they match the actual time. In this situation, adjusting just one clock to match the other two will not remove the error. 制作人: 故事里第三场在前。那时右袖被撕破，到第五场为止既没有换衣服，也没有修补。周五拍摄需要已经撕破的外套。
负责人: 如果只按拍摄日期顺序记录服装，就会出错。
制作人: 是的。请在拍摄日期旁边也记上故事中的场次和服装状态。实际后来才拍的场景中发生的变化，也可能需要在先拍的场景中呈现。撕破的位置也必须保持在右袖。

transcriptTurns.text: 计划本周五拍第五场，外套撕破的第三场下周再拍。既然还没拍撕破的场景，周五准备完好的外套就可以吗？

items.script:
Host: I heard that souvenir vouchers at this event can be reprinted and given to friends. Doesn’t that create a risk of collecting several times with the same voucher?
Organizer: Here, each issued number grants the right to one souvenir. Several sheets bearing the same number still represent just one right. Giving an unused voucher to a friend changes who can collect; it does not create a new right.
Host: Couldn’t you stamp the sheet they bring after handing over the souvenir and then return the sheet?
Organizer: Other printouts will not have that stamp, so that alone is insufficient. When handing over a souvenir, staff record that number as used. After that, reprinting the same number or bringing it in through another person does not allow another collection. Conversely, different unused numbers are not combined into one just because the same person brings them. We check which numbered rights remain, rather than whether the paper is new or who brings it.

主持人: 听说这个活动的纪念品兑换券可以重新打印，也可以送给朋友。这样不会有用同一张兑换券多次领取的风险吗？
组织者: 这里每个发放编号对应领取一份纪念品的权利。即使有多张印着同一编号的纸，这个权利也只有一份。把未使用的券送给朋友，只会改变由谁领取，并不会产生新的权利。
主持人: 发完纪念品后，在来人带来的纸上盖章，再把纸还给对方，不就可以了吗？
组织者: 其他打印件上没有那个章，所以仅靠这样还不够。工作人员发放纪念品时，会把该编号记为已使用。之后即使重新打印同一编号，或由别人带来，也不能再次领取。反过来，如果是不同的未使用编号，也不会因为由同一个人带来就合并成一份。核实的是哪些编号对应的权利还剩着，而不是纸是不是新的、由谁带来。

items.script:
Participant: Why aren’t you putting these sneakers and this small bag into the rubbish sack? They were all picked up by the river.
Operator: Finding things in the same place doesn’t mean we can immediately decide they were thrown away. For things with a name tag still attached or that seem to have been lost recently, we note their condition and set them aside for a while.
Participant: Do you keep these sneakers even though they’re wet?
Operator: Being wet alone doesn’t tell us whether the owner threw them away as unwanted. We’ll record their features and where they were found, put out a notice, and check during the set holding period whether anyone is looking for them.

Operator: That’s right. Rather than keeping them for a long time, the point is to allow time to check before disposing of things that could be returned.

items.script:
Host: The ends of the branches painted on the wall are empty. Is it not finished yet?
Creator: The painted part is finished. In the afternoon, the shadow of the nearby street tree overlaps that empty area. You can even see the leaves moving in the wind on the wall.
Host: Wouldn’t the picture seem less finished in the morning, when there’s no shadow?
Creator: I wasn’t trying to leave a picture that looks the same whenever you see it. I imagined an experience linking the morning’s empty space with the afternoon’s moving leaves. Rather than treating the tree as an obstacle behind the wall, I’ve let it become part of the work.
Host: I hear you came here on several days even before painting the wall.
Creator: Yes. I watched how far the shadow moved as time passed. That range helped me decide where to put the trunk on the wall. The connection is particularly clear on sunny afternoons, but its appearance on cloudy days is also part of the work.

items.script:
主持人: 墙上画出的树枝末端留着空白，是还没完成吗？
作者: 画出来的部分已经完成了。到了下午，旁边行道树的影子会叠在那块空白上，连叶子随风摇动的样子都能在墙上看到。
主持人: 上午没有影子时，会不会像一幅没画完的画？
作者: 我并不想留下无论何时看都相同的画，而是想让上午的空白与下午晃动的叶子形成连贯的体验。没有把墙后的树当作障碍，而是让它一起参与作品。
主持人: 听说画墙之前，您就来过这里好几天？
作者: 对。我观察影子随时间能移动到哪里，再根据范围决定墙上树干的位置。有阳光的下午连接尤其明显，不过阴天的样子也属于作品的一部分。

items.script:
Host: The ends of the branches painted on the wall are empty. Is it not finished yet?
Creator: The painted part is finished. In the afternoon, the shadow of the nearby street tree overlaps that empty area. You can even see the leaves moving in the wind on the wall.
Host: Wouldn’t the picture seem less finished in the morning, when there’s no shadow?
Creator: I wasn’t trying to leave a picture that looks the same whenever you see it. I imagined an experience linking the morning’s empty space with the afternoon’s moving leaves. Rather than treating the tree as an obstacle behind the wall, I’ve let it become part of the work.
Host: I hear you came here on several days even before painting the wall.
Creator: Yes. I watched how far the shadow moved as time passed. That range helped me decide where to put the trunk on the wall. The connection is particularly clear on sunny afternoons, but its appearance on cloudy days is also part of the work.

items.script:
Lecturer: Consider the sentence that a person transporting things came up the stairs empty-handed. When contrasted with someone carrying luggage, it means there was nothing in the person’s hands. But an article saying a negotiating team returned empty-handed may mean it failed to secure an agreement. The same expression can concern the presence or absence of different things.
Lecturer: Even a photograph of that team returning home with souvenir boxes need not contradict the article. The photograph shows objects in their hands, while the article may evaluate the negotiation’s outcome. items.script:
Reporter: The bottom of the screen behind the desk is open. Shouldn’t it reach the floor to block the wind?
Person in charge: That’s what we did at first. But when the wind blew on the test day, the paper blew around less while the whole screen was pushed strongly. So we kept the height where the books sit covered, but left a gap below for some wind to pass through.
Reporter: What did you check after making the gap?
Person in charge: We checked both how much the paper on the desk moved and how much the screen swayed. In this test, screen movement decreased without a large increase in paper blowing around. We didn’t call it a success merely because the bottom was open.
Reporter: Do you plan to use the same height at the next event?
Person in charge: If the desk height and wind conditions differ, we plan to test again. We don’t treat today’s result as a value that applies at every location.

记者: 桌后挡风屏下面是空的，要挡风不是应该一直垂到地面吗？

Host: In the directions exercise, you asked the listener to repeat the sequence they would follow. Were you checking whether they had memorized it exactly?
Instructor: Repeating identical words may not reveal what wasn’t understood. I asked them to point to their starting place and explain the route in their own words.

items.script:
Lecturer: Consider a fictional advertisement offering a small storage box when you buy a large container of detergent. If you already need the large container and have a use for the box, you can consider the benefit of receiving them together. But what if you buy the large container because the box is advertised as free, even though you have enough detergent at home? Although you do not pay separately for the box, you spend money on detergent to receive it. The word “free” does not mean this entire purchase costs nothing.
Lecturer: Here, rather than focusing only on the free gift, you should reconsider which items you need. If you need only the storage box, you can compare the cost of obtaining it separately with the total expenditure on buying the detergent as well. Counting leftover detergent just like something needed now, on the grounds that you will use it someday, obscures the comparison. Conversely, this does not mean people who need detergent should avoid the product merely because it comes with a gift. It is important first to identify the need and then compare ways of meeting it.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 세제를 큰 통으로 사면 작은 보관함을 준다는 가상 광고를 보겠습니다. 원래 큰 통이 필요하고 보관함도 쓸 곳이 있다면 함께 받는 혜택을 고려할 수 있습니다. 그런데 집에 세제가 충분한데도 보관함이 무료라는 말 때문에 큰 통을 사면 어떨까요? 보관함 가격은 따로 내지 않아도 그것을 받기 위해 세제 값은 지출합니다. 무료라는 표시가 이번 구매 전체에 비용이 없다는 뜻은 아닙니다.

items.script:
Commentator: This workshop makes display baseboards by joining two thin wooden boards. The following is a fictional experiment comparing production methods. In one group, the grain of both boards ran in the same direction; in the other, one board was rotated so the two grain directions crossed. After drying, the first group bent more to one side, while the second was relatively flat.
Maker: If the result were simply due to the increased thickness from joining two boards, we would have expected similar results in both groups. We kept the board type, thickness and amount of glue the same, and dried them in the same place for the same length of time. What we changed in this comparison was the relative orientation of the two boards.
Commentator: The maker did not immediately generalize the observation that the second group was flat to the properties of all wood. They began separately recording whether the same difference appeared with other thicknesses.

Commentator: This workshop makes display baseboards by joining two thin wooden boards. The following is a fictional experiment comparing production methods. In one group, the grain of both boards ran in the same direction; in the other, one board was rotated so the two grain directions crossed. After drying, the first group bent more to one side, while the second was relatively flat.
Maker: If the result were simply due to the increased thickness from joining two boards, we would have expected similar results in both groups. We kept the board type, thickness and amount of glue the same, and dried them in the same place for the same length of time. What we changed in this comparison was the relative orientation of the two boards.

items.script:
Lecturer: At a fictional meeting about whether to keep a small pond, three residents all supported preserving it. The first liked the view of the water, the second valued observing the pond’s small creatures up close, and the third spoke of memories of visiting with family. Three votes on the same side mean the choice is the same, not that the thinking behind it is identical.
Lecturer: Suppose a later amendment proposes keeping the pond but preventing people from going near the water. This directly affects the grounds of the person whose reason was observing the creatures. But we cannot conclude that this person will immediately oppose the proposal. They may accept observing from a distance, or have other reasons they did not initially mention. We must examine which reasons the changed conditions affect and ask again whether the person still supports the proposal.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 작은 연못을 남길지 논의하는 가상 모임에서 주민 세 명이 모두 보존안에 찬성했습니다. 첫 사람은 물이 보이는 풍경을 좋아했고, 둘째는 연못의 작은 생물을 가까이서 관찰하는 일을 중요하게 여겼습니다. 셋째는 가족과 다니던 장소라는 기억을 이야기했습니다. 세 표가 같은 쪽으로 모였다는 것은 선택이 같다는 뜻이지 그 선택에 이른 생각까지 하나라는 뜻은 아닙니다.

Lecturer: At a fictional meeting about whether to keep a small pond, three residents all supported preserving it. The first liked the view of the water, the second valued observing the pond’s small creatures up close, and the third spoke of memories of visiting with family. Three votes on the same side mean the choice is the same, not that the thinking behind it is identical.
Lecturer: Suppose a later amendment proposes keeping the pond but preventing people from going near the water. This directly affects the grounds of the person whose reason was observing the creatures. But we cannot conclude that this person will immediately oppose the proposal. They may accept observing from a distance, or have other reasons they did not initially mention. We must examine which reasons the changed conditions affect and ask again whether the person still supports the proposal.

items.script:
Host: One entry in this competition did not advance to the main judging stage. May we tell the artist it lacked artistic merit?
Judge: The work exceeded the announced maximum size. It was excluded at the initial specifications check and did not reach the main judging stage, where content and expression are assessed.
Host: The outcome is still rejection. Do we really need to distinguish the reasons?
Judge: Knowing which criterion led to the decision, and at what stage, helps with future preparation. If we convey a failure to meet the size requirement as a low score for the work’s content, we would be attributing an evaluation that was never performed.
Host: Then how about telling the artist the work is good in terms of content?
Judge: That is not something established by this decision either. We must clearly explain the reason for exclusion, along with the limit that the quality of the content was not assessed.

items.script:
Lecturer: An old shop newsletter says it closes on Mondays, while a new notice says it opens every day. Placed side by side, the two statements seem incompatible. But if the first describes last year’s operations and the second this year’s changed operations, both may be true for their respective periods. Before declaring either notice false simply because their contents differ, we must check whether they refer to the same period.
Lecturer: Another step is needed when using a notice to plan a visit now. A detailed notice with its date erased is not necessarily still valid. Conversely, an unreadable date alone does not establish that its contents are false. Ask the person in charge not only where the paper came from but also the start and end dates of the operations it describes. An old notice can be kept as a historical record, but its use must be distinguished from guidance for current visitors.

Customer: I want to put my name in my book, but I would like to avoid a method that could make ink smudge.

Staff member: Check whether the back of that page is also blank. If you choose a sheet blank on both sides, you can add your name without affecting the main text. When ordering, it would also be good to try pressing it on the same kind of paper as the actual book.

Planner: The statue is on a high pedestal, so its face is hard to see. Moving it to a lower pedestal at the entrance to the square would let people view it up close.
Records officer: I agree with letting people see it up close. However, this statue originally stood facing the old station. Moving it could erase the relationship that its orientation represented.
Planner: Then should we abandon the relocation plan?
Records officer: I am not saying we should prevent the move. How about recording its original location and the direction it faced on a small map? That could convey both the convenience of viewing it in the new location and the meaning of its old setting.
Planner: I will look into placing that map beside the new pedestal.

记录负责人: 我赞成让大家近距离观看。不过，这座雕像原来是面向旧车站站立的。换了位置，原来的朝向所表达的关系可能就消失了。
策划人: 那我们应该放弃迁移计划吗？
记录负责人: 我不是要阻止迁移。不如用一张小地图记录原来的位置和朝向，怎么样？这样既能传达新位置便于观看的好处，也能传达旧地点的意义。
策划人: 我会研究把那张地图放在新底座旁边的办法。

items.script:
Planner: The statue is on a high pedestal, so its face is hard to see. Moving it to a lower pedestal at the entrance to the square would let people view it up close.
Records officer: I agree with letting people see it up close. However, this statue originally stood facing the old station. Moving it could erase the relationship that its orientation represented.
Planner: Then should we abandon the relocation plan?
Records officer: I am not saying we should prevent the move. How about recording its original location and the direction it faced on a small map? That could convey both the convenience of viewing it in the new location and the meaning of its old setting.
Planner: I will look into placing that map beside the new pedestal.

items.script: Lecturer: Let us consider the statement, “Practice time was short. Even so, the performance went well.” Hearing the first sentence, you might expect the performance to have been difficult. But the next sentence gives a result different from that expectation. Here, 그래도 does more than merely indicate that two events happened in sequence. It expresses a relationship in which the earlier circumstances might have prevented the later result, but in fact did not. Nor does completing the performance well cancel the fact that practice time was short. Both the earlier circumstances and the later result hold true. When interpreting a connective, first consider what result the preceding statement leads you to expect.

transcriptTurns.textKo: “연습 시간이 짧았습니다. 그래도 연주를 잘 마쳤습니다.”라는 말을 보겠습니다. 앞말을 들으면 연주가 어려웠을 것이라고 예상할 수 있습니다. 그런데 뒤에서는 그 예상과 다른 결과를 말합니다. 여기서 그래도는 두 일이 차례로 일어났다는 표시만은 아닙니다. 앞의 사정이 뒤의 결과를 막을 법했지만 실제로는 그러지 않았다는 관계를 드러냅니다. 또 연주를 잘 마쳤다고 해서 연습 시간이 짧았다는 사실을 취소하지도 않습니다. 앞의 사정과 뒤의 결과가 모두 성립하는 상황이지요. 연결어를 이해할 때는 앞말로 어떤 결과를 기대하게 되는지 먼저 생각해 보십시오.

items.script:
Reporter: This is a map of the park paths that you read with your fingertips, but the branches seem farther apart than the actual paths. Is the scale wrong?
Map maker: At first, we reduced the spaces between the paths in the same proportions as in reality. But a user felt the two branches as a single line and missed the fork. After we widened the spacing, the user could identify where the path split.
Reporter: Then you can change the shape of the paths however you like?
Map maker: Not exactly. Which paths meet which, and the order in which you pass the forks from the entrance, remain unchanged. This map is not a tool for measuring distance; it is a resource for understanding the route in advance. We record the actual distance figures separately.

items.script: Lecturer: Today’s mobile is a model with a light rod suspended from the ceiling at one point and decorations attached on both sides. We will observe which side goes down once the swaying stops. One side may tilt even when there are equal numbers of decorations. That is because not only weight but also the distance from the rod’s suspension point to a decoration affects the result. Moving the same decoration outward increases its tendency to tilt that side downward; moving it inward reduces that tendency. Thus, we can bring the model closer to balance by adjusting positions without discarding a heavy decoration. In this model, let us assume that the length of the light thread holding a decoration changes only its height, not its attachment position on the rod. Observe carefully which part has been moved.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 오늘 모빌은 가벼운 막대의 한 점을 천장에 매달고 양쪽에 장식을 단 모형입니다. 흔들림이 멈춘 상태에서 어느 쪽이 내려가는지 보겠습니다. 장식 수가 같아도 한쪽이 기울 수 있습니다. 무게뿐 아니라 막대를 매단 점에서 장식까지의 거리도 영향을 주기 때문입니다. 같은 장식을 바깥쪽으로 옮기면 그쪽을 아래로 기울이려는 효과가 커지고, 안쪽으로 옮기면 작아집니다. 따라서 무거운 장식을 버리지 않고 위치를 조절해 균형에 가깝게 만들 수 있습니다. 이 모형에서는 장식을 단 가벼운 실의 길이는 높이만 바꾸고, 막대 위에서 장식을 단 위치는 바꾸지 않는다고 하겠습니다. 어떤 부분을 움직였는지 구별하며 관찰해 보십시오.

items.script: 演讲者: 今天的悬挂装饰模型，是把一根轻杆的某一点吊在天花板上，并在两侧挂上装饰物。我们来看看停止晃动后，哪一边会下沉。即使两边的装饰物数量相同，也可能向一侧倾斜。因为起作用的不只是重量，还有从杆的悬挂点到装饰物的距离。把同一个装饰物向外移，会增大使这一侧向下倾斜的作用；向内移则会减小。因此，不必扔掉重的装饰物，也可以通过调整位置，使模型更接近平衡。在这个模型中，我们假定悬挂装饰物的轻线长度只改变高度，不改变它在杆上的连接位置。请分清移动了哪个部分，再进行观察。

items.script: Lecturer: This museum makes replicas of old objects so that visitors can view them up close. Their size and surface patterns closely reproduce the originals, but the year of reproduction and the workshop are engraved in small letters on the underside. Putting that mark prominently in a place easily seen from above would change the appearance people view. Yet without any mark, an object could be mistaken for the original after it is separated from the exhibition. We therefore consider the presence of a mark separately from how conspicuous it is. Visitors can examine the original form, while those managing or moving the object can check the underside to identify its production history.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 이 박물관은 관람객이 가까이에서 볼 수 있도록 옛 물건의 복제품을 만듭니다. 크기와 표면 무늬는 원본에 가깝게 재현하지만 밑면에는 복제한 해와 제작소를 작게 새깁니다. 그 표시를 위에서 잘 보이는 곳에 크게 넣으면 감상할 모양이 달라집니다. 그렇다고 아무 표시도 없으면 전시에서 분리된 뒤 원본으로 오해될 수 있지요. 따라서 표시의 존재와 눈에 띄는 정도를 따로 생각합니다. 관람할 때는 원본의 형태를 살피게 하고, 물건을 관리하거나 옮길 때는 밑면을 확인해 제작 이력을 알아볼 수 있게 한 것입니다.

items.script: Lecturer: Can a record saying “The sound became louder than yesterday” establish that a space is too noisy for conversation? That statement merely compares yesterday’s sound with today’s. If it was originally very quiet, it might still not interfere with conversation after becoming louder. Conversely, even if the sound has become quieter, words might still be hard to make out. In the fictional study I will introduce today, having to ask again because an announcement was not understood on the first hearing was set as the criterion for interference with conversation. A record of sound increasing or decreasing tells us the direction of change, while whether the announcement was understood tells us whether the current condition meets the criterion. Distinguishing these prevents us from confusing the fact that improvement occurred with the judgment that the problem was solved.

transcriptTurns.textKo: “어제보다 소리가 커졌다”는 기록을 보고 그 공간이 시끄러워 대화하기 어렵다고 판단할 수 있을까요? 이 말은 어제의 소리와 오늘의 소리를 비교했을 뿐입니다. 원래 아주 작았다면 커진 뒤에도 대화에는 지장이 없을 수 있습니다. 반대로 소리가 줄었더라도 여전히 말을 알아듣기 어려울 수 있지요. 오늘 소개할 가상 조사에서는 안내 말을 한 번에 알아듣지 못하고 되묻는 상태를 대화 방해의 기준으로 정했습니다. 소리가 늘거나 줄었다는 기록은 변화 방향을 알려 주고, 안내 말을 알아들었는지는 현재 기준을 충족하는지 알려 줍니다. 둘을 구분해야 개선이 있었다는 사실과 문제가 해결됐다는 판단을 혼동하지 않습니다.

items.script: Lecturer: Can a record saying “The sound became louder than yesterday” establish that a space is too noisy for conversation? That statement merely compares yesterday’s sound with today’s. If it was originally very quiet, it might still not interfere with conversation after becoming louder. Conversely, even if the sound has become quieter, words might still be hard to make out. In the fictional study I will introduce today, having to ask again because an announcement was not understood on the first hearing was set as the criterion for interference with conversation. A record of sound increasing or decreasing tells us the direction of change, while whether the announcement was understood tells us whether the current condition meets the criterion. Distinguishing these prevents us from confusing the fact that improvement occurred with the judgment that the problem was solved.

items.script:
Host: Would viewers who cannot see the screen understand the story more easily if you also told them what the characters were thinking?
Writer: If I decide on a feeling that the work has not established, viewers lose the chance to interpret it differently. In this scene, a character smiles and then lowers their head. The dialogue does not give a reason for doing so.
Host: So instead of explaining that the character smiled out of regret, you describe the visible actions?
Writer: Yes. I convey the smile and the movement of lowering the head. I leave it open whether that reflects regret, playfulness, or another intention, so viewers can judge it together with the later scenes. Of course, that does not mean concealing information already established in the dialogue.

items.script: Lecturer: In a fictional costume room, someone said, “All the buttons in the blue storage box are made of fabric.” But one wooden button was found in that box and its material checked. That single button is enough to show that the original statement cannot stand as it is. The original statement included every button in the blue box without exception. However, we cannot change the conclusion to say that there are no fabric buttons in the blue box. The remaining buttons have not yet been checked. An observation sufficient to refute one claim is not necessarily sufficient to prove another universal claim that sounds like its exact opposite. We must examine precisely how far the discovered fact supports a conclusion.

items.script:
Staff member: The places where the dots were are visible in this book, but a reader said it is difficult to read. Should I mark them more darkly in black?
Repair specialist: This braille book is read by feeling raised dots with the fingertips. Long use has worn the dots down, so merely darkening the visible marks will not help.
Staff member: I see. Then work is needed to raise the dots again.
Repair specialist: Yes. In this book, different dot arrangements make different characters, so their original positions must be preserved. After repair, I will check both whether each dot can be distinguished by touch and whether the arrangement matches the original text.

items.script:
Host: You record the prototypes not only just after putting them on test strips, but later as well. Could repeatedly smelling the same scent make evaluators get used to it and perceive it differently?
Perfumer: That is why, in this fictional evaluation, a different evaluator who had never smelled that sample before took part at each time point. We kept the test strips, the quantity applied and the storage conditions the same. Both prototypes had a prominent floral scent at first, but later one left a grassy scent and the other a woody scent.
Host: If you had recorded only the initial floral scent, you would have summarized the two as similar.
Perfumer: Exactly. I want to examine separately whether the initial impression is pleasant and what scent it develops into over time. Different lingering scents do not automatically mean a production failure either. They are evidence for checking whether the progression matches what we intended.

items.script: Lecturer: Even with the same words, what is excluded changes depending on where the particle 만 is attached. In today’s examples, we will compare only the scope expressed in the sentences, without adding omitted context. 민수만 책을 빌렸다 limits the people who borrowed books to Minsu. It does not say whether Minsu also borrowed other things. By contrast, 민수가 책만 빌렸다 limits what Minsu borrowed to books, but does not determine whether anyone else borrowed books. Using the same name and the word book does not mean the two sentences exclude the same alternatives. First find the part to which the particle is attached, and then consider alternatives to that part.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 같은 낱말을 써도 조사 만을 어디에 붙이는지에 따라 제외하는 대상이 달라집니다. 오늘 예문에서는 생략된 앞뒤 상황 없이, 문장에 적힌 범위만 비교하겠습니다. 민수만 책을 빌렸다는 말은 책을 빌린 사람을 민수로 제한합니다. 민수가 다른 물건도 빌렸는지는 말하지 않습니다. 반면 민수가 책만 빌렸다는 말은 민수가 빌린 것을 책으로 제한하지만, 다른 사람이 책을 빌렸는지는 정하지 않습니다. 이름과 책이라는 낱말이 같다고 해서 두 문장이 같은 대안을 제외하는 것은 아닙니다. 조사가 붙은 부분을 먼저 찾고, 그 부분과 비교될 대안을 생각해 보세요.

items.script:
Reporter: Many fish photographs were collected in a fictional observation project. The research team did not publish the number of photographs directly as the number of fish. Let us hear why.
Researcher: For the fish in this study, we stipulated that right-side body patterns differ between individuals and do not change during the study period. The same patterns appeared again in photographs from several dates. These may be records of seeing the same individuals again rather than newly increased numbers of fish.
Reporter: If you group them as the same individual, do you discard some photographs?
Researcher: No. When and where the fish was seen again is also observational information, so we retain it. However, our current comparison catalog contains only right-side photographs. We have not established whether the left and right patterns are the same, so we cannot directly match left-side photographs against the right-side catalog.

items.script:
Stage-effects maker: Blowing air under the red fabric and shining a light on it makes it look like flames when viewed from the seats. This device does not use real fire.
Colleague: It worked well when tested on its own, but the actor opens and reads a paper letter here. We should try that scene with it too.
Stage-effects maker: Since there is no fire, wouldn’t it be enough just to check whether we can bring the paper close?
Colleague: If the air moving the cloth also shakes the letter, it could alter the actor’s action of opening and reading it. I want to check whether it works with the actual movement and props while preserving the effect seen from the seats. A device working well alone is different from the whole scene proceeding smoothly.

items.script: Lecturer: In this class, we define a triangle as a closed figure made of three straight line segments meeting at their endpoints. If a textbook repeats only the same shape with one vertex pointing upward, learners sometimes memorize that orientation or equal side lengths as conditions for the name. So we also show figures with three unequal sides and figures rotated sideways. These examples preserve the defining conditions while changing only the familiar appearance. Conversely, we also examine a figure that looks pointed at the top but has one curved side. This checks the habit of grouping things based only on a rough impression of similarity. The aim of showing varied figures is not to increase the number of pictures to memorize. It is to have learners explain which differences change the name and which leave it unchanged.

items.script: Commentator: This fictional musical device made for an exhibition reads holes in a paper roll. The lateral track containing a hole determines its pitch, and the note sounds when the moving paper carries that hole past the reading line. The device plays every hole in the order it passes, and we test within a speed range where it misses no holes even when the paper moves faster. With the same roll fed slowly and quickly, the holes’ lateral positions and passing order were unchanged. What changed was the time before the next hole reached the reading line. Preserving the arrangement of notes on paper had not also fixed the performance to a single tempo. For the exhibition, we therefore record the feed speed used at the time separately from the replica roll.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 전시용으로 만든 이 가상 연주 장치는 종이 롤의 구멍을 읽습니다. 가로로 어느 줄에 구멍이 있는지가 음의 높이를 정하고, 종이가 앞으로 움직여 구멍이 읽는 선을 지날 때 그 음이 납니다. 구멍을 지나는 순서대로 빠짐없이 소리가 나도록 만들었으며, 종이가 빨라져도 구멍을 놓치지 않는 범위에서 시험합니다. 같은 롤을 느리게 보냈을 때와 빠르게 보냈을 때에는 구멍의 가로 위치도, 지나는 순서도 같았습니다. 다만 다음 구멍이 읽는 선에 도달하기까지 걸리는 시간이 달라졌습니다. 종이에 적힌 음의 배열을 보존했다고 해서 연주의 빠르기까지 한 가지로 보존한 것은 아니었던 셈입니다. 전시에서는 롤의 복제본과 별도로 당시 사용한 이동 속도도 기록해 둡니다.

items.script: 解说员: 这台为展览制作的虚构演奏装置会读取纸卷上的孔。孔在横向哪一列，决定音高；纸向前移动，孔经过读取线时便发出该音。装置按孔经过的顺序逐一发声，测试时限定在纸加快也不会漏孔的速度范围。同一纸卷慢送和快送时，孔的横向位置和经过顺序都相同，改变的只是下一个孔到达读取线所需的时间。保留纸上音符排列，并不等于连演奏速度也固定为唯一一种。因此展览除了纸卷复制品，还另行记录当时使用的送纸速度。

items.script: Commentator: This fictional musical device made for an exhibition reads holes in a paper roll. The lateral track containing a hole determines its pitch, and the note sounds when the moving paper carries that hole past the reading line. The device plays every hole in the order it passes, and we test within a speed range where it misses no holes even when the paper moves faster. With the same roll fed slowly and quickly, the holes’ lateral positions and passing order were unchanged. What changed was the time before the next hole reached the reading line. Preserving the arrangement of notes on paper had not also fixed the performance to a single tempo. For the exhibition, we therefore record the feed speed used at the time separately from the replica roll.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose meeting records include both requested tasks and the responses to them. In response to a request to send materials by tomorrow, the person in charge said they would send them. This response confirms acceptance of the request. It does not confirm that the materials have actually arrived. Moving an entry from accepted to completed merely because the next day has come creates a fact not present in the record. Conversely, failing to find a delivery record does not justify changing the earlier acceptance to refusal. Unconfirmed performance is different from there having been no promise at all. Record requests, acceptance and execution in connection with one another, but include evidence for each stage. Which stages have not yet been verified is also part of the record.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 모임 기록에 부탁한 일과 그에 대한 응답을 함께 적는다고 해 봅시다. 자료를 내일까지 보내 달라는 요청에 담당자가 보내겠다고 답했습니다. 이 답변으로 확인한 것은 요청을 받아들였다는 사실입니다. 자료가 실제로 도착했는지까지 확인한 것은 아닙니다. 다음 날이 되었다는 이유만으로 수락 칸을 완료 칸으로 옮기면 기록에 없던 사실을 만들어 냅니다. 반대로 도착 기록을 찾지 못했다고 앞선 수락도 거절로 고쳐서는 안 됩니다. 실제 실행이 확인되지 않은 상태와 약속 자체가 없었던 상태는 다르기 때문입니다. 부탁, 수락, 실행을 서로 연결해 남기되 각 단계의 근거를 적어야 합니다. 어떤 단계를 아직 확인하지 못했는지도 기록의 일부입니다.

items.script:
Host: Even though there is no wall onstage, pushing with your hands makes it look as if there is one. Is the shape of a hand exerting force the key?
Performer: That shape matters too, but focusing on one push misses something. If the right hand goes much farther back than the plane the left hand touched, the movements no longer give the impression of touching the same wall.
Host: So individual actions can look clear yet conflict with each other.
Performer: That is why, when handling the same object continuously in a scene, I maintain its initially established position and size in the next action too. No real object stops my hands, so I must maintain that relationship myself. If the scene moves the object, I also have to show the process of moving it.

items.script: Lecturer: Two people edited the same story file separately. A changed a character’s name from Narae to Bora, while B added a line calling Narae in another paragraph. Because the edited lines did not overlap, the merging tool displayed no conflict. Yet the merged text introduced the same character as Bora while retaining dialogue calling them Narae. Sentences that were natural in each individual file were not guaranteed to remain natural after merging. Overlapping lines concern editing locations; whether one change affects the interpretation of another expression concerns relationships in the content. Discarding the whole new line or merely changing the save order does not examine that relationship. We must find expressions that depend on other information, then reconcile them while preserving the intentions of both edits.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 이야기 파일 한 개를 두 사람이 따로 고쳤습니다. 가는 인물의 이름을 나래에서 보라로 바꾸었고, 나는 다른 문단에 나래를 부르는 대사를 새로 넣었습니다. 두 사람이 손댄 줄은 겹치지 않아 합치는 도구는 충돌 표시를 내지 않았습니다. 그렇지만 합친 글에는 같은 인물을 보라라고 소개하면서 나래라고 부르는 대사가 남았습니다. 각자의 파일에서 자연스럽던 문장이 합친 뒤에도 자연스럽다는 보장은 없었던 것이죠. 줄이 겹쳤는지는 편집 위치의 문제이고, 한 수정이 다른 표현의 해석에 영향을 주는지는 내용 관계의 문제입니다. 새 대사를 통째로 버리거나 저장 순서만 바꾸어서는 이 관계를 검토한 것이 아닙니다. 어떤 표현이 다른 정보에 기대고 있는지 찾은 뒤, 두 수정의 의도를 살리면서 함께 맞춰야 합니다.

Woman: For now, focus on direction rather than force. Try sending it into that large area several times, and once you get used to it, make the target a little smaller.

items.script:
Patron: Why have you covered both the titles and authors’ names on these books? That seems to make choosing a book harder.
Staff member: Some people said they tend to look only for names they already know. In this activity, readers look only at the first sentence and choose one book that appeals to them. The idea is to respond to the sentence itself first.

Staff member: No. Once a book is chosen, the wrapping is removed and its cover and description can be checked. If you have already read it or it is not a book you want, you do not have to borrow it. items.script:
Host: In the door-knocking scene, you repeat the same character “똑,” meaning a knock, but the spaces between the characters differ. Does that show how loud the sounds are?
Cartoonist: In this scene, I used character size for loudness and the spacing between characters for the time between knocks. I wanted to distinguish one loud knock from several quick knocks.
Host: So small characters close together would mean quiet but rapid sounds.
Cartoonist: Yes. But I am not saying this is a rule that applies equally to every comic. In this work, I used the two devices consistently so that readers would not have to guess their meaning again in every scene.

Man: Clearing guests’ plates as soon as they are empty would make tidying up faster.
Woman: But some guests may be waiting a moment to get more food. An empty plate does not necessarily mean the meal is over.
Man: Then shall we clear them when guests put down their spoons and chopsticks?
Woman: Here, we have not assigned a meaning to the position of the spoons and chopsticks. Guests might put them down just to talk for a moment. Why not ask whether we may clear the plate? I mean we should not mark the meal as finished before hearing the answer.

Host: I heard you raised the notes because the main melody was getting lost in the ensemble. Are you still using the higher notes?
Arranger: No. That method changed the piece’s range, so I returned to the original pitches. Instead, I tried playing the main melody on a different instrument producing the same notes.
Host: Did it make a difference even at the same pitch?
Arranger: Yes. In the recordings we compared this time, the sharp timbre stood apart from the soft accompaniment, making the melody easier to follow. We kept loudness and pitch the same because we wanted to see the effect of changing instruments. But this does not mean that any timbre will stand out against every accompaniment.

items.script: Lecturer: Someone in a workroom said, “내일 여기서 마무리하겠습니다.”, meaning “I will finish here tomorrow.” Suppose this was quoted word for word in a library the following day. Inside the quotation, 내일, or tomorrow, still means the day after the original utterance, and 여기, or here, means the workroom where it was originally said. It does not become the library where the person quoting it is standing. By contrast, without quotation marks, the message can be adapted to the current situation as: “That person said they would finish in the workroom today.” Keeping the wording unchanged and preserving what it refers to are not the same task. First checking when, where and as whose words an expression was spoken helps avoid mistakenly moving the quoted place to the present location.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 누군가 작업실에서 “내일 여기서 마무리하겠습니다.”라고 말했습니다. 이 말을 다음 날 도서관에서 그대로 인용했다고 해 봅시다. 따옴표 안의 내일은 여전히 처음 말한 날의 다음 날이고, 여기는 처음 말한 작업실입니다. 인용하는 사람이 서 있는 도서관으로 바뀌지 않습니다. 반면 따옴표를 없애고 현재 상황에 맞추어 전하려면, 그 사람은 오늘 작업실에서 마무리하겠다고 했다고 풀어 말할 수 있습니다. 문구를 그대로 보존하는 것과 지시 대상을 보존하는 것은 같은 작업이 아닙니다. 언제 어디서 누구의 말로 한 표현인지 먼저 확인해야 인용 속 장소를 현재 장소로 잘못 옮기는 일을 피할 수 있습니다.

items.script:
Reporter: The doll in the middle of the image is still, while only the wall pattern behind it moves sideways. Is this a device that rotates the wall?
Maker: The wall is fixed to the floor. We secured both the camera and the doll to a rotating platform so that their distance and orientation relative to each other would not change. When the platform turns, the doll moves within the room, but its relation to the camera stays the same.
Reporter: So keeping the same place in the image does not mean it is also stationary within the room.
Maker: Exactly. A separate camera placed on the floor shows that same doll rotating. In any footage, we must check what the reference for judging motion is attached to. Using image position alone could make us reverse which of the wall and doll is actually moving relative to the floor.

items.script:
记者: 画面中央的人偶不动，只有后面的墙面图案向旁边移动。这是让墙旋转的装置吗？
制作者: 墙固定在地面上。我们把相机和人偶一起固定在旋转台上，让两者之间的距离和相对朝向保持不变。转台旋转时，人偶也在房间里运动，但它与相机的关系不变。
记者: 原来在画面中保持位置，不代表在房间里也静止不动。
制作者: 是的。用另放在地面的相机拍摄，就能看到同一个人偶在旋转。无论看哪段影像，都要确认判断运动的参照固定在哪里。只看画面内位置，可能把墙和人偶中究竟哪一个相对地面运动判断反了。

items.script:
Actor: I play both the delivery person and the homeowner. Do I have to keep the scarf on even when the delivery person is angry?
Director: Yes. Early in this performance, we establish that a scarf means the delivery person and no scarf means the homeowner. If you take it off because the character is angry, the audience may think the role has changed too.
Actor: Then, when I am the delivery person, must my tone also stay gentle as it was at first?
Director: There is no need for that. The scarf identifies who the person is, while the tone of voice conveys how that person feels now. The character can be angry while still being the delivery person. Let us use separate devices for maintaining the character’s identity and expressing changes within that character.

items.script: Lecturer: The sentence “할머니께서 오셨어.”, meaning “Grandma has arrived,” includes expressions honoring Grandma. That does not mean the speaker is also speaking formally to the listener. The ending 어 is a style used with someone close. Conversely, “친구가 왔습니다.”, meaning “A friend has arrived,” does not use a form that specially honors the friend, but it is formal toward the listener. In one sentence, how the person being talked about is treated and how the listener is addressed are two different directions. Therefore, a politely ended sentence does not necessarily honor every person mentioned within it. We need to check separately whose action has an honorific expression and whom the sentence ending addresses. The style chosen in actual conversation should take relationships and circumstances into account, but today we are looking at the point that these two directions need not match.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose only the short answer “Eunseo” has been recorded. If it followed a question asking who sent a letter, it means Eunseo was the sender. But if it followed a question asking whom the letter was sent to, Eunseo refers to the recipient. The answer sounds the same and contains the same name, but the preceding question requires it to fill a different slot. In actual conversation, the participants have heard that question together, so they can understand without repeating at length who sent the letter or to whom it was sent. That does not mean a record with the response isolated from the question retains all the same information. We cannot call a conversation incomplete merely because words were omitted, nor can we call a context-free record sufficient merely because there was a short answer. We need to check what shared information filled in what was omitted.

Participant: If we take all the pieces out of the sand and lay them in a row, numbering them will be easier.
Coordinator: Wait a moment. In this activity, we examine not only the shapes of the objects but also how they were positioned in relation to one another. Before taking them out, record their locations and orientations and attach numbers.
Participant: If we number them afterward, will we be unable to tell whether it is the same piece?
Coordinator: We may still be able to identify a piece itself, but there will be no record of which piece it was originally beside or which way it was facing. A number is a label linking the object to the record. It cannot create a record of an arrangement that was never recorded.

items.script:
Customer: One rib of my umbrella has broken, but the fabric is intact. I can keep using the fabric, right?
Staff member: If possible, I will replace just the rib. However, even parts of the same length can have their fabric-attachment loops in different positions.
Customer: So matching the length is not enough.
Staff member: Right. I will first look for a part whose loop positions match the attachment points on the existing fabric. The fabric being untorn is a good sign, but that does not mean we have checked whether it will attach properly to the new part.

items.script:
Host: I can see the paths left by tools on the surface. Did you stop before smoothing it out?
Sculptor: This part is finished as it is. I carved shallow marks across deeper ones. I wanted viewers to follow the sequence in which my hands moved.
Host: Then you leave any scratches that occur during the work.
Sculptor: Not quite. I repair scratches made during transport because they are unrelated to the sequence of work I chose. An uneven surface alone does not make something unfinished, and the mere presence of marks does not make all of them artistic expression.

items.script:
Man: If you hide names during judging, won't it be hard to explain afterward to each person why they received their score?
Woman: The works can be numbered, with the reasons for the assessment recorded under each number. A separate coordinator can keep the table linking names and numbers.
Man: If the judges can see that table, hiding the names will be less effective.
Woman: That is why I propose keeping it inaccessible to them until the assessments are finished. Once the results are decided, the coordinator sends the reasons listed under each number to the corresponding entrant. Keeping identities unknown during judging and explaining the grounds for decisions afterward can be handled through different information at different times.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 이름을 가리고 평가하면 나중에 왜 그런 점수를 주었는지 개인별로 설명하기 어렵지 않나요?

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose a shared workshop has a rule, ‘장비를 사용한 뒤에는 사용 기록을 한 줄씩 남긴다’ (Leave one line in the usage log after each use of the equipment). The coordinator explains it as ‘사용할 때마다 기록한다’ (Make a record every time it is used). Here, what counts as a repetition is one occasion of use, not a date. If it was used on two separate occasions on the same day, each use gets its own record; on a day when it was not used, this rule does not require creating a usage entry. Thus, shortening the wording to ‘매일 한 번 기록한다’ (Make one record every day) changes the criterion. That would combine several uses in a day into one and require an entry even on a day with no use. On the other hand, just one line in a day's usage log does not establish that the equipment was used exactly once that day. If we do not yet know whether every use was recorded without omissions, a missing entry remains possible. What the rule requires and evidence that it was actually followed must be checked separately.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 공동 작업실에 “장비를 사용한 뒤에는 사용 기록을 한 줄씩 남긴다”는 규칙이 있다고 합시다. 담당자는 이를 “사용할 때마다 기록한다”고 설명했습니다. 여기서 반복을 세는 기준은 날짜가 아니라 사용한 한 차례입니다. 같은 날 두 차례 따로 사용했다면 기록도 각각 남기지만, 사용하지 않은 날에 이 규칙 때문에 사용 기록을 만들지는 않습니다. 따라서 이 말을 “매일 한 번 기록한다”로 줄이면 기준이 달라집니다. 하루에 여러 번 사용한 경우를 하나로 합치고, 사용이 없던 날에도 기록을 요구하는 셈이니까요. 한편 사용 기록이 하루에 한 줄 있다는 사실만으로 그날 장비를 꼭 한 번만 썼다고 단정할 수도 없습니다. 모든 사용이 빠짐없이 기록되었는지 아직 모른다면 기록 누락 가능성이 남습니다. 규칙이 요구하는 것과 실제로 지켜졌다는 증거는 따로 확인해야 합니다.

items.script: 演讲者: 假设共享工作室有一条规定：‘장비를 사용한 뒤에는 사용 기록을 한 줄씩 남긴다’（每次使用设备后，都留下一行使用记录）。负责人把它解释为‘사용할 때마다 기록한다’（每用一次就记录一次）。这里计算重复次数的单位是一次使用，而不是日期。如果同一天分两次使用，就分别留下记录；没有使用的日子，不会因为这条规定而制作使用记录。因此，如果简化成‘매일 한 번 기록한다’（每天记录一次），标准就变了。这样等于把一天多次使用合成一次，并且连没有使用的日子也要求记录。另一方面，仅凭一天的使用记录只有一行，也不能认定当天一定只用过一次。如果还不知道每次使用是否都毫无遗漏地记录下来，就仍可能存在漏记。规定要求什么，与是否有证据证明实际遵守了规定，需要分别确认。

The coordinator explains it as ‘사용할 때마다 기록한다’ (Make a record every time it is used). Here, what counts as a repetition is one occasion of use, not a date. If it was used on two separate occasions on the same day, each use gets its own record; on a day when it was not used, this rule does not require creating a usage entry. Thus, shortening the wording to ‘매일 한 번 기록한다’ (Make one record every day) changes the criterion. That would combine several uses in a day into one and require an entry even on a day with no use. On the other hand, just one line in a day's usage log does not establish that the equipment was used exactly once that day. If we do not yet know whether every use was recorded without omissions, a missing entry remains possible. What the rule requires and evidence that it was actually followed must be checked separately.

evidenceSpans.quoteKo: 같은 날 두 차례 따로 사용했다면 기록도 각각 남기지만, 사용하지 않은 날에 이 규칙 때문에 사용 기록을 만들지는 않습니다.
evidenceSpans.quote: If it was used on two separate occasions on the same day, each use gets its own record; on a day when it was not used, this rule does not require creating a usage entry.

evidenceSpans.quoteKo: 모든 사용이 빠짐없이 기록되었는지 아직 모른다면 기록 누락 가능성이 남습니다.
evidenceSpans.quote: If we do not yet know whether every use was recorded without omissions, a missing entry remains possible.

items.script: 演讲者: 假设共享工作室有一条规定：‘장비를 사용한 뒤에는 사용 기록을 한 줄씩 남긴다’（每次使用设备后，都留下一行使用记录）。负责人把它解释为‘사용할 때마다 기록한다’（每用一次就记录一次）。这里计算重复次数的单位是一次使用，而不是日期。如果同一天分两次使用，就分别留下记录；没有使用的日子，不会因为这条规定而制作使用记录。因此，如果简化成‘매일 한 번 기록한다’（每天记录一次），标准就变了。这样等于把一天多次使用合成一次，并且连没有使用的日子也要求记录。另一方面，仅凭一天的使用记录只有一行，也不能认定当天一定只用过一次。如果还不知道每次使用是否都毫无遗漏地记录下来，就仍可能存在漏记。规定要求什么，与是否有证据证明实际遵守了规定，需要分别确认。

transcriptTurns.textKo: 공동 작업실에 “장비를 사용한 뒤에는 사용 기록을 한 줄씩 남긴다”는 규칙이 있다고 합시다. 담당자는 이를 “사용할 때마다 기록한다”고 설명했습니다. 여기서 반복을 세는 기준은 날짜가 아니라 사용한 한 차례입니다. 같은 날 두 차례 따로 사용했다면 기록도 각각 남기지만, 사용하지 않은 날에 이 규칙 때문에 사용 기록을 만들지는 않습니다. 따라서 이 말을 “매일 한 번 기록한다”로 줄이면 기준이 달라집니다. 하루에 여러 번 사용한 경우를 하나로 합치고, 사용이 없던 날에도 기록을 요구하는 셈이니까요. 한편 사용 기록이 하루에 한 줄 있다는 사실만으로 그날 장비를 꼭 한 번만 썼다고 단정할 수도 없습니다. 모든 사용이 빠짐없이 기록되었는지 아직 모른다면 기록 누락 가능성이 남습니다. 규칙이 요구하는 것과 실제로 지켜졌다는 증거는 따로 확인해야 합니다.

items.script:
Reporter: There are three gears of the same size connected in a row. Since the first and last turn in the same direction, does that mean the middle gear is not transmitting the rotation?
Maker: The external teeth of the three gears mesh directly in sequence. Seen from the same side, neighboring gears that mesh turn in opposite directions. The direction reverses once from the first to the second, then again from the second to the third, so the two ends turn the same way.
Reporter: Then even if you add one more gear, the last one will still turn the same way as long as the first is turned in the same direction.
Maker: Adding another connection in which external teeth mesh in sequence adds one more reversal. When a middle gear is removed, the remaining gears also need to be brought back into mesh. You must not calculate as if rotation is transmitted to a gear that is disconnected. Here, first check that they are all connected, then follow each meshing point to determine the directions in sequence.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 같은 크기의 톱니바퀴 세 개가 한 줄로 이어져 있네요. 첫 바퀴와 마지막 바퀴가 같은 방향으로 도니 가운데 바퀴가 회전을 전달하지 않는 건가요?

transcriptTurns.text: There are three gears of the same size connected in a row. Since the first and last turn in the same direction, does that mean the middle gear is not transmitting the rotation?

items.script:
记者: 三个大小相同的齿轮排成一行连在一起呢。第一个和最后一个转动方向相同，是不是说明中间的齿轮没有传递转动？
制作者: 三个齿轮的外齿依次直接啮合。从同一侧看，相互啮合的相邻齿轮转动方向相反。从第一个到第二个反转一次，从第二个到第三个又反转一次，所以两端的方向相同。
记者: 那即使再加一个齿轮，只要第一个仍向同一方向转，最后的方向也不会变吧。
制作者: 每增加一处外齿依次啮合的连接，就会多一次反转。取走中间齿轮时，也需要把剩下的重新啮合起来。不能把转动当成会传到脱离连接的齿轮上。这里要先看是否全部相连，再沿着各处啮合依次判断方向。

items.script:
Reporter: I saw material saying the library is considering relocating. I have made the first question, ‘When will you move to the new building?’
Editor: That question could be taken to mean that a decision to move has already been made. Doesn't the material only say that possible locations are being examined?
Reporter: If they answer that they do not know the date, wouldn't that tell us it is still undecided?
Editor: That answer alone does not distinguish between a move that is decided with only the date unresolved and a move that is itself still undecided. First ask whether a decision has been made to relocate; if the answer is yes, then ask about the timing. Adding a question mark does not make unverified content disappear from the sentence.

items.script:
记者: 我看到一份材料说图书馆正在考虑搬迁。我把第一个问题定为‘什么时候搬到新楼？’。
编辑: 这个问题可能会让人以为已经决定搬迁了。材料不是只说正在考察候选地点吗？
记者: 如果回答不知道日期，不就能知道还没确定吗？

items.script:
Reporter: I saw material saying the library is considering relocating. I have made the first question, ‘When will you move to the new building?’
Editor: That question could be taken to mean that a decision to move has already been made. Doesn't the material only say that possible locations are being examined?
Reporter: If they answer that they do not know the date, wouldn't that tell us it is still undecided?
Editor: That answer alone does not distinguish between a move that is decided with only the date unresolved and a move that is itself still undecided. First ask whether a decision has been made to relocate; if the answer is yes, then ask about the timing. Adding a question mark does not make unverified content disappear from the sentence.

items.script: Lecturer: A person who missed a train says, “If I had left a little earlier, I would have caught that train.” The statement mentally rewinds the actual situation and imagines a different possibility. In this situation, leaving early and catching the train is not something that happened; it is what the person imagines with regret. That does not mean the person never set foot outside the house. They may have left, but not early enough. Nor does this statement say whether they took a bus or waited for the next train after missing it. The imagined alternative outcome, the fact that it did not actually occur, and what the person did afterward need to be considered separately. A single expression of regret should not be expanded into a record of the person’s entire day of travel.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 기차를 놓친 사람이 “좀 더 일찍 떠났더라면 그 기차를 탔을 텐데”라고 말합니다. 지금의 실제 상황을 이야기 속에서 되돌린 뒤 다른 가능성을 떠올리는 말이지요. 이 상황에서 일찍 떠나 기차를 탄 것은 실제로 일어난 일이 아니라 후회하며 그려 본 일입니다. 그렇다고 집에서 한 발도 나오지 않았다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 출발은 했지만 충분히 이르지 않았을 수 있습니다. 또한 기차를 놓친 뒤에 버스를 탔는지, 다음 기차를 기다렸는지는 이 말에 들어 있지 않습니다. 과거와 다른 결과를 생각했다는 점, 그 결과가 실제로는 이루어지지 않았다는 점, 그 뒤의 행동이 무엇인지는 각각 나누어 들어야 합니다. 후회하는 말 한마디를 하루 전체의 이동 기록으로 늘려서는 안 되겠지요.

Commentator: This is not a specimen for measuring the age of an actual tree. It is an imaginary model that represents time with bands. The maker used the center point as the first boundary and drew three circles outside it.
Maker: The interval from the center to the first circle is defined as year one, from the first circle to the second as year two, and from the second to the third as year three. A boundary itself is not a year; the interval between adjacent boundaries represents a year.
Commentator: The bands have different widths. Could a wide band represent two years?
Maker: In this model, one band represents one year regardless of width. Also, if the center is covered, the number of visible bands alone cannot determine the whole period. You need to know which numbered circle the last visible circle is in order to include the concealed period.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose you receive a recommendation letter while looking for someone to put in charge of planning an event. The letter describes in detail how the person is punctual for appointments and is polite when working with others. However, it does not mention experience developing an event plan or drawing up a budget. That alone does not justify concluding that the person cannot plan an event. The writer may never have worked with them on that task. Conversely, plentiful praise does not establish that their planning ability has been verified. Receiving a positive impression is not the same as obtaining the evidence needed for this role. Rather than converting the recommendation’s wording into a low score, you can ask further about what the person actually did in the planning process. Do not fill what was left unsaid with negative facts, but do not mistake the gap for the evidence you need either.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 행사 기획을 맡길 사람을 알아보려고 추천 편지를 받았다고 합시다. 편지에는 약속 시간을 잘 지키고 함께 일할 때 예의가 바르다는 말이 자세히 적혀 있습니다. 그런데 행사를 구상하거나 예산을 짠 경험은 언급되지 않았습니다. 이것만으로 그 사람이 기획을 못한다고 결론낼 수는 없습니다. 추천인이 그 일을 함께 해 보지 않았을 수도 있으니까요. 반대로 칭찬이 많다는 이유로 기획 능력까지 확인되었다고 할 수도 없습니다. 긍정적 인상을 받는 일과 이번 역할에 필요한 근거를 얻는 일은 같지 않습니다. 이때는 추천 문구를 낮은 점수로 바꾸기보다, 기획 과정에서 실제로 어떤 일을 했는지 추가로 물어볼 수 있습니다. 말하지 않은 부분을 부정적 사실로 채우지 않되, 그 공백을 필요한 근거로 착각하지 않는 태도가 필요합니다.

items.script:
Host: The pulley exhibit has a wheel fixed to the ceiling and another that moves with the object. Both raise the object by pulling a rope. How do they differ?
Designer: I will explain using a model that excludes friction, rope stretching and the pulley’s own weight. A fixed pulley changes only the direction of the force. If lifting the object directly requires one hundred newtons, the rope also needs a pull of one hundred newtons, and it is pulled through the same distance as the object rises. With a pulley that moves with the object and is supported by two sections of rope, the required force falls to fifty newtons. In exchange, you must pull twice the distance that the object rises.
Host: Since less force is needed to raise the same object to the same height, switching to a movable pulley makes the motor’s other conditions less important, then.
Designer: We cannot really view it that way. In this model, the force is halved but the pulling distance doubles, so their product is unchanged. It still has the advantage of potentially allowing a motor with a smaller maximum force. However, the rope-winding mechanism must be able to take in the full length required. Even with sufficient force, a limited pulling distance can prevent reaching the target height. We must choose between the two arrangements by considering both the motor’s force and the rope-travel limit.

items.script:
主持人: 滑轮展品里，有固定在天花板上的轮子，也有随物体一起移动的轮子。两种都是拉绳子把物体提起来，有什么区别呢？
设计者: 我用一个忽略摩擦、绳子伸长以及滑轮自身重量的模型来说明。定滑轮只改变力的方向。如果直接提起物体需要一百牛顿，拉绳子也需要一百牛顿的力，拉过的绳长与物体上升的高度相同。如果由两段绳子支撑随物体移动的滑轮，所需的力就降到五十牛顿。相应地，要拉过相当于物体上升高度两倍的绳长。
主持人: 把同一个物体提到同一高度时更省力，那么换成动滑轮后，电机的其他条件就不那么重要了吧。
设计者: 不能这样看。在这个模型里，力减半，但拉动距离加倍，所以两者的乘积相同。不过，它仍有可能让最大拉力较小的电机也能使用，这是一个优点。但卷绳装置必须能把所需的绳长全部卷入。即使力足够，如果能拉动的距离太短，也无法达到目标高度。选择这两种方式时，必须同时看电机的力和绳子移动距离的限制。

items.script: Lecturer: An imaginary device releases colored cards one at a time. The first four were red, blue, red, blue. You might infer a rule that alternates red and blue; call this rule 가. But a rule that repeats a five-card group of red, blue, red, blue, blue, which we will call 나, also gives the same first four cards. Even if we reset the device to its initial state and observe just those four cards repeatedly, the two candidates remain indistinguishable. All repeated observations giving the same result is different from establishing that only one rule can produce that result. To distinguish the two candidates, we can check the fifth card, where their predictions diverge. Rule 가 will release red, while 나 will release blue. If the fifth card is red, 나 is inconsistent with the result among the two candidates presented here. This does not mean that no other rule could match 가 for the first five cards and differ afterward. We must distinguish which candidate among those compared has been eliminated from whether all possible rules for the device have been established.

items.script:
Host: In this piece, you turn quickly and then remain still for quite a while. Is that a rest after a difficult movement?
Dancer: I do steady my breathing, but I am not trying to look as though I am resting. Even while my body is still, I keep looking in the direction my arm points and retain the tension of a movement about to begin. This is a section that makes the audience anticipate the next movement.
Host: Should a pause caused by losing your balance midway also be understood as that kind of expression?
Dancer: Only the visible fact of briefly stopping is the same. If my gaze wavers as I regain my balance, the flow between the preceding and following movements breaks. In rehearsal, I do not just time the stillness; I also examine where I look and the energy carrying me into the next movement.

transcriptTurns.textKo: 이번 작품에서는 빠르게 돌다가 오랫동안 멈추시더군요. 어려운 동작 뒤에 쉬는 시간인가요?

舞蹈家: 我确实会调整呼吸，但不是为了让人看出我在休息。身体虽然停住，视线仍看着手臂所指的方向，也保留着动作即将开始时的张力。这一段会让观众期待下一个动作。
主持人: 如果中途失去平衡而停下来，也可以看作这种表达吗？

Host: Beside the photos of the same food taken on different dates, you also have notes about its aroma and texture. If the photos were sharper, would the writing still be needed?
Photographer: In this record, the aroma changed even between two days when the appearance was similar, and the feel when pressing the surface changed too. Regardless of how sharp a photo is, those differences are hard to tell just by looking.
Host: Then are the notes more important than the photos?

items.script:
Host: Beside the photos of the same food taken on different dates, you also have notes about its aroma and texture. If the photos were sharper, would the writing still be needed?
Photographer: In this record, the aroma changed even between two days when the appearance was similar, and the feel when pressing the surface changed too. Regardless of how sharp a photo is, those differences are hard to tell just by looking.
Host: Then are the notes more important than the photos?
Photographer: It is not a matter of ranking one above the other. Photos preserve shape and color; the notes preserve other qualities I sensed that day. We need to connect records from the same dates to compare visible changes with changes sensed in other ways.

items.script:
Discussant A: You said anyone could submit a layout proposal. If the safety officer makes the final decision, does that not diminish the point of seeking opinions?
Discussant B: Our group agreed to arrange the stage using proposals that leave the aisle at least as wide as the specified standard. Suggestions help us find different ways to use the space, and the officer is responsible for checking whether those proposals meet the standard.
Discussant A: So even a popular proposal has to be revised if its aisle is too narrow.
Discussant B: Yes. But the officer must not dismiss a proposal simply by saying they do not like it. They need to explain which part of the layout fails which standard so that the person who submitted it can revise it. Distinguishing the opportunity to propose from the responsibility to decide does not deny the value of opinions.

items.script: Lecturer: Suppose a work report lists Friday as the planned completion date for the props and Saturday as the current forecast completion date. The different dates do not mean that one is a typo. In this report, the planned date is the date in the team’s work plan, while the forecast date is an estimate based on the current pace of progress. The team can be striving to finish as planned while forecasting a day’s delay at the current pace. If a report of a changed forecast is read as approval of a change to the plan, it becomes unclear whether the original target is still in place. Conversely, reporting an unchanged outlook simply because the target date remains unchanged conceals the possibility of a delay. If the plan has been changed, that decision should be recorded separately. We should communicate what we intend to do separately from what we think will happen.

items.script:
Reporter: In this activity, we look at the rod placed in front of us with one eye at a time. The rod appears to overlap different patterns on the wall behind it. Has the rod moved?
Staff member: The rod and wall are fixed in place. Since our eyes are apart, the starting point from which we view them differs. Photos taken by cameras in two positions in this setup show the same difference.
Reporter: Then we would need two cameras to record this difference.
Staff member: If the object and background remain fixed, we can move one camera between two positions to take the photos. items.script:
Host: In the results of a fictional race, one participant’s ranking changed from third to second. Does that mean their recorded time was corrected to a faster one?
Commentator: That is possible, but the ranking alone does not tell us. In this case, the participant’s time stayed the same, and one person ahead of them was excluded from the results. The ranking rose because the comparison group changed.
Host: Then can we tell the ranking from the time?
Commentator: We also need the other participants’ times and to know who is included in the results. Even with the same finishing time, the ranking changes depending on who the person is compared with. How long the person took and where they stand among those included in the results complement each other, but they are not the same information.

主持人: 在一场虚构比赛的结果中，一名参赛者的名次由第三变成了第二。这是不是说明该参赛者的成绩被改成了更快的时间？
解说员: 有这种可能，但只看名次无法知道。在这个例子中，该参赛者的用时没变，是排在前面的一人不再计入结果。比较对象变了，名次才会上升。
主持人: 那么，看用时就能知道名次吗？
解说员: 还要知道其他参赛者的用时以及哪些人被计入结果。即使用时相同，和谁比较也会影响名次。自己用了多久，与在计入结果的人当中排在哪里，两种信息互相补充，却不是同一种信息。

Commentator: That is possible, but the ranking alone does not tell us. In this case, the participant’s time stayed the same, and one person ahead of them was excluded from the results. The ranking rose because the comparison group changed.
Host: Then can we tell the ranking from the time?
Commentator: We also need the other participants’ times and to know who is included in the results. Even with the same finishing time, the ranking changes depending on who the person is compared with. How long the person took and where they stand among those included in the results complement each other, but they are not the same information.

items.script: Lecturer: When we hear that a cup has been filled almost to the brim, we can imagine that little empty space remains. But that does not determine how many milliliters short of full it is. Saying that the seats at an event are almost all taken also conveys that the venue is close to full, but does not say exactly how many seats remain. It does not tell us which rows the remaining seats are in, either. In this way, “almost” indicates closeness to some reference point, which varies according to what is being discussed. items.script:
Commentator: Two skirts made with the same fabric and shape are hanging here. They look similar at rest, but when the actor spins and stops, one hem drops quickly while the other keeps swaying longer. In this fictional demonstration, only the positions of the small weights attached inside the skirts were varied.
Costume maker: The total weight added to each skirt is the same. In one, the weights are spread around several points on the hem; in the other, they are gathered at one point higher up. If we assume the movement will be the same because we added the same weight, we miss this difference.
Commentator: So photographs of the outward appearance and the weight would not be enough for the costume inventory.
Costume maker: Right. This time, we needed to see how the hem followed after the actor stopped. We recorded where the weights were attached and checked the movement in the actual scene. Which version is better depends on the effect wanted for that scene.

items.script: Lecturer: Let us look at the Korean expression “누가 그걸 모르겠어요,” meaning “Who wouldn’t know that?” If someone says this when the other person repeats a well-known fact and then moves to another topic, it can be understood as emphasizing that everyone knows that much, rather than asking for the name of someone who does not. Having the form of a question does not always mean that a sentence requests information. However, this utterance is not evidence that everyone’s knowledge has actually been surveyed. It only shows that the speaker treats the fact as widely known. In contrast, if someone asks “누가 아직 설명을 못 들었습니까,” meaning “Who has not heard the explanation yet?”, and waits for people to raise their hands, there are grounds for viewing it as a question intended to identify those who have not heard it. It is important to judge the function of an utterance from its form and the surrounding actions, without turning what it emphasizes into a fact established through inquiry.

items.script:
Host: The Korean clue in the puzzle story grew from one sentence to two in the translation. Is there a reason?
Translator: The original uses two meanings of the same written form, “눈”: snow and eye. Readers have to discover that both the snowflake decoration and the eye-shaped picture in the room are relevant. On another page of the story, they can learn the order: touch the snowflake first, then the eye picture.
Host: If the target language has different words for the two objects, using just one name would be difficult.
Translator: That is why I created clues that bring each of the two objects to mind. But I did not explain the order here as well. I wanted to preserve the structure in which readers identify the objects and work out the order separately. What mattered more than matching the number of sentences was neither leaving out needed information nor giving it ahead of time.

items.script: Lecturer: A choir introduction states that, among the members who joined this year, Seoyeon has been active in this choir the longest. The comparison is limited to members who joined this year. It does not mean Seoyeon has been active longer than someone who joined ten years ago. Meanwhile, if we say that Seoyeon’s time in this choir has become longer than their earlier time in another choir, that compares two of Seoyeon’s own experiences. Ranking among people and change between one person’s experiences are different dimensions. Even knowing both does not automatically establish the ranking within the entire current choir or the exact number of months of participation. Removing “among the members who joined this year” to shorten the introduction expands the scope of the comparison being claimed. To preserve the scope of the information, we must retain which group the comparison concerns and which of the same person’s experiences are being compared.
